note: Post-pilot design review (workflow post-pilot-design-review, 2026-10-09): four assessment lenses with their own experiments (evolution/search, task/world, cell rules, development), three critics scoring every proposal, and the synthesis (docs/POST_PILOT_CALLS.md). Experiment scripts lived in the session scratchpad and are not kept.

assessed.lens:
Evolution and search. Seven new experiments, all with life seeds from base 36,100,000 + 100,000 x 1 and its sub-blocks (36.100M-36.104M); scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-jgon-project-ml-cell-dev/aefb0c66-3af5-49c4-936c-154d6434706c/scratchpad/review/evo/.
- E1 econ.py: income and cost split, 128 lives.
- E2 popgen.py / run_popgen.sh / purge.py: fixation probability and purging under seven selection schemes.
- E3 takeoff.py: the mutant neighbourhood of stuck v1 clickers in v1 and in SPECK.
- E4 lmax.py: the same genomes at L_max 4 and L_max 2, 128 paired lives.
- E5 dfe.py: distribution of mutational effects (DFE) for three operators, 40 mutants x 40 lives.
- Log analyses traj.py, founders.py, runlevel.py.
- load.py is a discarded model: symmetric mutation effects overpredict progress about 100x.

Headline: in SPECK, search mostly works. The evolved bodies already compute with lateral messages, and the best of them catch as many targets as the tuned reflex. They fail the routing criterion mainly because they pay for twice the cells, a small-effect trait that selection barely sees. Two things limit progress: evolution sits close to mutation-selection balance (each child about 0.19 F worse than its parent), and each run makes one attempt. Ranking noise is not the bottleneck. v1 fails at the start for three reasons: founders win a lottery, the clicker's foothold is lost, and ties freeze the population.

working.item: SPECK lets unseeded evolution start and climb reliably.
working.evidence: 10/10 seeds grow and 7/10 reach F >= +4. The founders are genuine: the census has 0.30-0.53% of genomes at F >= 0 (v1: 0.07-0.15%), and generation-0 parents have mean F +0.09 to +0.46. Five of the 10 runs grew straight from their founders: median size >= 6 cells by generation 1-5 in s0, s2, s4, s7 and s9 (traj.py). No SPECK run lost its clicker; the clicker sits +0.48 F above the lone cell.

working.item: Evolution finds local message-passing computation, and it is where the fitness is. The best bodies match the tuned reflex in skill.
working.evidence: Spearman 0.71 between F and the share of F that lateral messages carry. E1 (128 lives) splits each gap to reflex@hollow3 (F 8.37, income 9.95, 20.4 captures, 45 misses, 56 cells) into income and cost. s5: income 9.65 (-0.31), 19.8 captures, 19.9 misses. s6: income 9.61 (-0.34), 19.7 captures, 16.2 misses. They catch as much as the reflex with 2.3-2.8x fewer misses. Neighbour voting, cooperative detection with feedback inhibition, and gain set by crowding are all evolved local algorithms.

working.item: Bounded growth is selected without a target in the competent lineages.
working.evidence: The five best SPECK bodies (s4-s8) stop by T/2 (share still growing 0.00-0.02); the five worst keep growing. The n_view contact brake evolved in every unseeded lineage (n_view knockout sends the body to the 1,024-cell guard). This is what 'optimal from physics plus costs' predicts: the marginal cell pays only in poor bodies.

working.item: Selection does see small effects across generations, so a 0.03 rank correlation does not mean a lottery for new beneficial mutations.
working.evidence: E2 simulates the exact 256x3 > 64x4 > 32 scheme with per-life sd 2.0, 8.5% broken children and heritable background load. A new child with true advantage delta fixes with P = 0.045 / 0.092 / 0.138 / 0.254 / 0.458 at delta = 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5 / 1.0 F, against about 0.0025 for a neutral one (only 3 fixations in 1,200 runs, so that baseline is rough). That is roughly P_fix = 0.45 x delta: carriers are re-tested every generation. The 0.03 correlation instead reflects a converged shortlist (true sd about 0.16 F; one breed; mean pairwise distance about 3.5).

working.item: The two-stage recheck and CRN are worth what they cost.
working.evidence: purge.py, one generation with the measured DFE: the pilot scheme gives D = +0.024 F per generation. 256x2 > 64x5 gives +0.018 (about equal per life). The cheaper schemes pass load: one stage 256x3 -0.005, 256x1 > 64x3 -0.008, lam96 +0.005. In the audit verdict, recheck lives are 1.2-2.0x as productive as a third first-pass life. CRN is decisive for small bodies (paired sd 0.0015 at 2 cells).

working.item: Runs are predictable mid-way and still improving, so longer and selective continuation is cheap headroom.
working.evidence: runlevel.py: Spearman between valid F around a generation and final F is 0.21 at generation 50, 0.58 at 100, 0.79 at 200 and 0.94 at 300. The valid-F slope over generations 300-499 has a median of +0.45 F per 100 generations (s5 +0.66, s7 +0.35, s1 +1.22, s3 +1.02); only s0, s2 and s4 have plateaued (+0.03 to +0.19).

not_working.item: v1 unseeded takeoff: 6/10 seeds stay at 1-2 cells.
not_working.evidence: The founders are a lottery: the best founder scored +0.06 to +0.15 on 2 lives, and in 4/13 v1 runs (L4 s1, s2, s4, s7) the population was 99-100% lone cells by generation 10. Same founders, different fates: L2 s2 and L4 s2 have identical founder censuses (lives are identical below z = 2), yet L2 s2 grew at generation 53 while L4 s2 lost its clicker. Clicker populations that kept the clicker took off at generations 14, 53, 168, 191 and 338: 5 takeoffs in about 2,264 run-generations, roughly 1 per 450 generations (about 1 per 100,000 children). E3 used the 2-cell clicker populations of v1 L4 s0 and s3, with 384 mutants each from four operators, on 6 lives in both worlds. 0.5-4.4% of mutants grow to 4 or more cells, but only 5 of 3,072 mutant tests in v1 and 0 of 3,072 in SPECK were growers that were significantly better. The best mutants were all 2-cell tweaks (v1 +0.03 to +0.06; SPECK +0.23 to +0.38). SPECK populations that settled on a clicker (s1, s6, s8) took off after another 60-140 generations, about 3x v1's rate.
not_working.likely_cause: (1) v1's clicker edge over the lone cell (+0.044, per-life sd 0.08-0.11; 33-42% of its lives score at or below the lone cell) is within noise. Under CRN, one bad set of shared lives makes every clicker lose to genomes that score exactly the lone value. (2) A canalised clicker has no uphill growth mutants nearby, so takeoff waits for rare multi-step events. SPECK avoids both because its founders already include multi-cell earners and its foothold is about 10x larger.

not_working.item: Frozen plateaus from the tie rule (still in the code).
not_working.evidence: v1 L4 s1, s2, s4 and s7 kept zero children for 244, 285, 364 and 356 generations. src/evolve.py:516 puts parents first ([pop, kids]), and the sorts at :523, :361 and :368 are stable, so on the exact lone-cell value (-0.02) parents always win.
not_working.likely_cause: A stable sort with parents first switches off neutral drift exactly where drift is the only way out. Critique item evo-2 is confirmed by the pilot and still unfixed.

not_working.item: 0/10 routers: the gap to the tuned reflex is mostly cell upkeep, not skill.
not_working.evidence: E1, gap to reflex@hollow3 split into income, living cost and other costs. s5: -1.67 = -0.31 income, -1.18 living, -0.19 other. s6: -2.36 = -0.34, -2.15, +0.13. s7: -1.91 = -1.22, -0.75. s8: -2.43 = -1.72, -0.74. s5 and s6 carry 115 and 163 cells (body mean), against 56 for the reflex and 122 for router@ring4. They pay for a router-sized body but earn reflex income: router income is 13.69 at 122 cells. E4: the same genomes in catch_speck_l2 (no hidden planes) score s6 +0.86 ± 0.27 (z 3.2), s9 +0.56 ± 0.20 (z 2.8), s5 +0.50 ± 0.30, s2 +0.23, s7 +0.21, s4 -0.06, s8 -0.05 (mean +0.32 F). Hidden cells are inert everywhere.
not_working.likely_cause: Each superfluous cell costs 0.02 F. Removing 5 cells (+0.1 F) has P_fix of about 0.045 per variant (E2), and the change is often coupled to development, so economy drifts. The tuned reflex was found with coordinate ascent on 192 lives per candidate. Reaching the router's crisp relay roles from s5's soft recruitment probably needs coordinated changes: removing its feedback inhibition costs -5.6 F and lets the sense sheet run away; emit1 knockout costs -11.7. A hypothesis, not tested. The GS3 dip from the hand reflex is not the binding barrier, because no evolved lineage passes through the tuned reflex.

not_working.item: Near mutation-selection balance: slow late progress.
not_working.evidence: E5 (s5 best, 40 mutants x 40 lives, SE about 0.35 per mutant). The standard operator: mean dF -0.19 per child (non-broken -0.14), 3% broken (< -2 F), 10% significantly deleterious, 0/40 significantly beneficial (top +0.71). Knockout: mean -0.90, 7% broken, 23% deleterious, 1/40 beneficial. Row-scale: mean -1.10, 15% broken, 25% deleterious, 1/40 beneficial; the 1/40 is consistent with the 2.3% false-positive rate. Valid F rises about 0.005 F per generation after generation 300 (audit), while each generation must purge about 0.19 F of load just to stay level.
not_working.likely_cause: Near-neutral mutations are mostly slightly deleterious, and beneficial ones of 0.3 F or more are rare. Most selection effort goes into holding position. Critique item evo-5 is weakened as a default: knockout and row-scale are 5-6x more destructive per child on working genes, with no detectable gain in beneficial mutants (also none from stuck clickers in E3).

not_working.item: One attempt per run: early collapse to one breed, an uninformative founder screen, large between-run variance.
not_working.evidence: All runs fall to one breed by generation 2-119. The winning breed's founder screen ranks are 0, 0, 1, 1, 3, 6, 6, 6, 6, 7 of 0-7 (runlevel.py), so the 2-life screen does not pick the winner. Final F has a between-run sd of 1.52 F (mean 5.02, range 2.66-7.06). s4 plateaued from generation 100 (4.2-5.1) while s6 started last (0.3 at generation 100) and finished at 6.22.
not_working.likely_cause: Uniform mating over 32 parents in one pool, and no restart or continuation mechanism. src/run.py cannot resume a run, so promising runs cannot be extended and stuck ones cannot be re-founded.

not_working.item: Expressivity that exists but is locked or unused.
not_working.evidence: Exactly 8 active genes in every unseeded best and 5 in every seeded one (duplication rate is 0). The seeded genome secretes at -800, so chemistry knockout is exactly 0 in every seeded best. p_die knockout is 0.00 everywhere. Hidden planes are inert and cost up to 0.86 F (E4).
not_working.likely_cause: The search space as configured cannot add genes. The neutral playground that silent duplicates would give is switched off. Hidden planes have no task value in SPECK, and L_max 4 is the user's design.

not_working.item: How the pre-pilot critique's evolution items stand after the pilot.
not_working.evidence: evo-1 (records and racing): weakened. Pooling the parents' previous lives changed fixation probability within noise (E2: 0.92-1.13x; audit: under 2% more selection differential). Racing at 256x2 > 64x5 is 0.93-1.25x per life, about +8% on average. evo-2 (ties): supported; fix now. evo-3 (demes): supported in its diagnosis, but small demes risk drift load near balance, so prefer run-level portfolios. evo-4 (founders): supported for v1, weakened for SPECK. evo-5 (mixed operator): weakened as a default (E5). evo-6 (duplication): untested; still the best route to new structure. neuro hidden-plane item: strengthened (E4). simplify faster-conduction item: supported (pilot: router +1.99, reflex +0.99, evolved bodies +0.14 to +1.70).
not_working.likely_cause: n/a (status summary)

proposals.title: Protect the first foothold: random tie-breaking, size-adaptive lives, founder re-screen and founder size cap
proposals.change:
Four changes, all in src/evolve.py and the configs:
(1) Break ties at random with a dedicated generator: a permutation key before each of the three stable sorts. Trajectories without ties stay bitwise the same. Add kids_kept and n_tied to the curves rows.
(2) Size-adaptive lives: choose each generation's L as clamp(round(B / c), 3, 32), where c is last generation's mean events (or CPU) per life and B is a fixed per-generation budget, for example the pilot's cost at L = 3 for 60-cell bodies. One L per generation, so CRN is kept. 2-cell generations get about 32 lives almost free (0.0016 CPU-s per life against 0.15-0.25 at 120 cells), and late generations stay at 3 + 4.
(3) Founder re-screen: the top 256 of the 16,384 live 12 more shared lives (about 3k lives). Seed from the best, preferring distinct phenotypes (end size, whether they click) and preferring multi-cell earners.
(4) Founder lives get their own n_max 256: 4.8-5.3x fewer events, and the same top 8 in two batches tested.
proposals.targets: v1 takeoff (6/10 at 1-2 cells), the loss of the clicker in 4/13 v1 runs, frozen plateaus, and founder-lottery picks; it also speeds up early SPECK.
proposals.evidence: Frozen 244-364 generations in v1 L4 s1, s2, s4 and s7 (tie rule at src/evolve.py:516/523). The clicker's edge over the lone cell is +0.044 against per-life sd 0.08-0.11; with 32 lives its SE is about 0.018 (z about 2.4) instead of 0.04 at 7 lives. E3: from a canalised clicker, no uphill growth mutant turned up in 3,072 tests per world, so keeping founders that already grow matters more than waiting. In SPECK, 5/10 runs grew straight from their founders. The founder screen's ranking does not predict the winning breed (ranks 0-7). Founder time is 50-71% of the wall time of stuck runs.
proposals.expressivity: Nothing is lost. More multi-cell lineages survive the first generations to be explored.
proposals.constraints: Harness and selection only: no organism rule, no clock, no global channel inside a life. Fitness is unchanged. Within the standing approval of minor tweaks.
proposals.cost: About 60-100 lines in evolve.py plus tests (forced ties, an L schedule that keeps CRN, a founder-only world override). Test compute is small: 2-cell v1 generations take about 1 s, so 10 seeds x 500 generations is a few CPU-hours, or about 1 h on the laptop.
proposals.test: Pre-register on v1 L4, 10 seeds x 500 generations: at least 6/10 seeds leave 4 or fewer cells (pilot 4/10); no run keeps zero children for more than 50 generations; no run is more than 90% lone cells at generation 10 (pilot 4/13). On SPECK L4 (6 seeds x 150 generations), median generation to 6 cells not later than the pilot's (pilot median 32).

proposals.title: Checkpoint and resume, then run-level successive halving and extension instead of fixed one-shot runs
proposals.change: Add checkpoint and resume to src/run.py and evolve_life: population, ids and origins, the torch generator state, the generation, and the curves offset, saved every 25 generations. Then run exploratory searches as a portfolio. For example, launch 16 seeds; at generation 200 keep the top 8 by mean valid F over generations 180-200; at 400 keep the top 4; extend those to 1,000 or more. Separately, extend the four best pilot SPECK runs (s5, s7, s6, s8) from their final populations to 1,000 generations. Pre-registered count criteria still use the full fixed seed set; the portfolio serves discovery ('one such seed is the first evolved router').
proposals.targets: One attempt per run, early local optima (s4), still-climbing runs cut at 500, and spot or rental readiness.
proposals.evidence: Runs are predictable mid-way: Spearman 0.79 at generation 200 and 0.94 at 300. The late slope has a median of +0.45 F per 100 generations, with s5 at +0.66: at that pace s5 would reach the reflex's +8.69 in about 250 more generations if the slope holds (an extrapolation). Between-run sd is 1.52 F. The audit notes run.py cannot resume, so spot capacity loses whole runs. Halving is worth about 25-40% of compute against running all 16 to the end.
proposals.expressivity: Nothing changes in the organism. Search reaches further along the lineages that work.
proposals.constraints: Harness only; a selection-level choice across runs, outside any life. The resume must be bitwise: test that a resumed run equals an uninterrupted one. No user approval needed.
proposals.cost: About 100-150 lines plus a bitwise resume test. Extending 4 runs by 500 generations at about 175 CPU-s per generation is about 100 CPU-h: about 1 h on a 192-core spot box (about $4-6), or a few days on the laptop.
proposals.test: Resumed equals uninterrupted (curves and best genome byte for byte). Extension of s5, s7, s6 and s8 to 1,000 generations, pre-registered: at least 1 of 4 reaches F above reflex@hollow3 by more than 3 SE on 1,024 fresh lives, or income above the reflex's income by more than 3 SE with lateral_off removing at least half of the lead. Report cell counts and how many generations each needed.

proposals.title: Keep the 3 + 4 two-stage selection; take only the exact speedups; no parent records, no 1-life first stage
proposals.targets: The 'selection rank correlation 0.03' question and the cheapest fix with the same selection quality.
proposals.evidence: E2 fixations per life relative to the pilot, across delta 0.1-1.0: 256x2 > 64x5 0.93-1.25; lam96 0.95-1.12; one stage 0.89-1.04; parent records 0.92-1.13 (the same per generation); 4x lives 0.44; 256x1 > 64x3 1.52-1.70. Purge with the measured DFE (mean -0.19 per child): the pilot +0.024 F per generation, 2 + 5 +0.018, one stage -0.005, 256x1 > 64x3 -0.008. The cheapest scheme lets through about 0.03 F per generation of load, 6x the observed net progress of 0.005, so its fixation gain is likely cancelled. The audit verdict agrees: 2 + 5 keeps 92-98% of the gain at 1.14-1.21x, and it found that the models overpredict real progress 10-30x.
proposals.expressivity: Unchanged.
proposals.constraints: Harness only. The fast-mode hash hazard: gates and golden tests must keep the full build.
proposals.cost: Fast mode was already measured by the audit (small kernel flag work). The optional A/B: 2 arms x 10 seeds x 300 generations, about 15 h on a 192-core spot box (about $50-80). Only worth it if compute is the binding constraint.
proposals.test: The exact speedups: a fixed set of evolution runs is bitwise identical, with the expected 1.5-1.7x less CPU per generation. The A/B, if run: median final valid F of 2 + 5 is not lower than 3 + 4 by more than 0.3 F, at 19% fewer lives.

proposals.title: Make routing worth more than economy noise: faster conduction now, L_max 2 for S1 if the user agrees, and an income readout for routing
proposals.change:
(a) World constants d0 0.5 and d_min 0.25, with delay_sd and jit kept as fractions. Re-tune the hand references and rerun GS1-GS6.
(b) Ask the user whether S1 runs at L_max 2 (preset catch_speck_l2), bringing hidden planes back when a stage needs depth.
(c) Add a reported, not judged, routing readout: income lead over reflex@hollow3 on 1,024 lives, plus the lateral_off share of that lead. This separates computation from cell economy.
proposals.targets: 0/10 routers. Bodies sit at reflex income with router-sized bodies, so the selective signal for relays is small next to the economy noise.
proposals.evidence: Pilot fast-conduction forks: router +1.99, reflex +0.99, so the router's lead grows from +2.27 to about +3.3 F. Evolved bodies gain +0.14 to +1.70; s6, the most lateral-dependent, gains +1.70. E2: P_fix grows about linearly with delta (0.25 at 0.5 F, 0.46 at 1.0 F), so a larger step makes relays easier to select. E4: hidden cells cost s6 +0.86 (z 3.2), s9 +0.56 (z 2.8), s5 +0.50, mean +0.32 over 7 bests, and are inert everywhere. E1: s5 and s6 already earn 9.65 and 9.61 against the reflex's 9.95, so an income readout would show how close the skill is.
proposals.expressivity: d0 changes latency only; delta delay lines still allow slow paths. L_max 2 removes unused hidden planes for S1 only; they return at S2. The readout adds no rule.
proposals.constraints: (a) is a world calibration that adds no clock or rule, but it re-prices every gate: record it as a section-15 tweak. Arguably within the standing approval, though d_min also shortens notices and claims, so re-check growth timing. (b) L_max 4 is the user's design and needs the user's approval. (c) Changing the pre-registered criterion is the user's call; propose it as reported only.
proposals.cost: (a) A gate rerun and re-tune: about 3-4 CPU-h. One SPECK arm, 10 seeds x 500 generations, about 240 CPU-h (about 1.5 h on a 192-core box, $6-16). (b) Config only. (c) About 30 lines in scripts/catch_pilot_analysis.py.
proposals.test: Pre-register for a SPECK arm at d0 0.5 against the pilot (10 seeds each): the number of seeds whose final best is a router under the existing criterion (A2 and A4 against a reflex re-tuned at the new delay) is greater than 0; the median lateral_off share is at least the pilot's; median F is not lower. For L_max 2 (if approved): median final cells lower, F not lower.

proposals.title: Turn on silent gene duplication, and point the large mutation steps only at silent, not-yet-wired genes
proposals.change: Set dup_rate 0.02, del_rate 0.01 and dup_split false (a bitwise-neutral copy), as the design's step 6 planned. In LifeLayout.mutate, apply row-scale (exp(N(0, 0.7)) on a gene's W row and b) and occasional large single-entry steps only to genes whose outgoing W column and A column are all zero (silent duplicates). Their row can drift and sharpen neutrally until an ordinary mutation wires them. Working genes keep the gentle N(0, 0.5) operator. Seeded arms use handbuilt.catch_reflex_genome(), with secretion near -5 instead of -800, so chemistry is one mutation away.
proposals.targets: Fixed 8-gene capacity (the GRN router uses 13); switch or latch genes that the gentle steps never build (evolved self-weights below 4); seeded arms locked at 5 genes and with no chemistry; the mutation load that blocks structural moves.
proposals.evidence: E5 on the s5 best: knockout and row-scale applied to working genes cost -0.90 and -1.10 F per child (7% and 15% broken), against -0.19 for the standard step, with no detectable beneficial excess (1/40, about the false-positive rate). A useful structural operator must therefore not land on working genes. Silent copies are bitwise neutral (genome tests). Every unseeded best has exactly 8 active genes and every seeded best 5. Seeded bests' chemistry knockout is exactly 0 (secretion -800).
proposals.expressivity: Adds evolvable capacity: more genes, crisp role logic and new channels of regulation. Nothing is removed.
proposals.constraints: Genome and search operators only; the organism's rules are unchanged. A genome that never duplicates lives bitwise as before. Targeting 'silent' genes uses only the genome, not the life. Within the minor-tweak remit; tell the user, since gene count was fixed in practice.
proposals.cost: About 40 lines in src/genome.py plus tests (a targeted step is phenotype-neutral until wired; duplicate registry). A/B with 6 SPECK seeds x 500 generations per arm: about 300 CPU-h (about 2 h on a rented 192-core box).
proposals.test: Pre-register: active genes above 8 in at least 4/6 seeds by generation 500; mean per-child load (an E5-style DFE on the final best, 40 x 40) no worse than -0.25 F; median final F not lower than the matched control by more than 0.3 F; report genes with self-weight of 4 or more and their role (knock out each such gene).

proposals.title: Per-life task variety through the existing per-life world draw, as stepping stones, a generalisation test and more information per CPU-second
proposals.change: Extend LifeEvaluator's per-life envelope draw (it already keys noise physics by run, purpose, generation and life, shared by every genome) to task keys: sigma in {0.6, 1.0, 1.5}; v_t in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}; number of simultaneous targets in {1, 2, 3} (new world key); R_cap/c_miss ratio held at 50. Fitness stays the mean F over lives. Keep a fixed held-out task set (unseen combinations) for generalisation. Later, the per-life task family can grow (other CATCH variants, then FOLLOW and READ worlds) without changing the loop.
proposals.targets: Fragile early gradients (SPECK lineages grow; v1 lineages starve), generalisation across situations (the user's goal), and Poisson capture noise per CPU-second.
proposals.evidence: In SPECK 10/10 seeds grow and in v1 4/10: a mixture keeps SPECK's strong foothold while v1 lives reward a wide sense disk. Per-life noise is capture-count Poisson (sd about 0.49 x sqrt(19) = 2.1 F; within-genome correlation of F with captures 0.99), so more targets per life means more captures per life. CPU is linear in cell-time; receptor candidates are 43-60% of heap events, about 4% accepted. A multi-target life costs more receptor events, but information grows with the capture count: an estimated 1.5-2x per CPU-second at 3 targets, not measured. CRN is preserved because the draw is per life index.
proposals.expressivity: Adds a world feature (several targets) and variety. Bodies must generalise; nothing in the cell model is removed. A body specialised for one halo size may score lower, which is intended.
proposals.constraints: A task and world change (multiple targets is a new world rule; the draw is world-side, so no cell reads it and no global channel enters a life). Needs the user's approval as a task decision, in line with the stated aim of more task variety later. Gates for the new key (multi-target capture accounting) and GS-style references are needed.
proposals.cost: Kernel work for more than one target (target arrays, receptor sums, capture bookkeeping) of moderate size, plus the reference or invariant tests and gate references. Evaluator config is small. The first test is 10 seeds x 500 generations on rented cores, about $10-20.
proposals.test: Pre-register against SPECK-only runs at equal lives: F on the held-out task set higher by more than 3 SE in the median seed; at least as many seeds growing by generation 100; per-life sd of F divided by mean captures lower; SPECK-only F not lower than the SPECK arm by more than 0.5 F.

assessed.lens: Task and world design (CATCH/SPECK). My own experiments are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-jgon-project-ml-cell-dev/aefb0c66-3af5-49c4-936c-154d6434706c/scratchpad/review/task/. Scripts: worlds.py, analyse_worlds.py, cloud.py, analyse_cloud.py, surround.py, sizeopt.py. Outputs are in out/: worlds_summary.txt, retention.txt, cmiss_reprice.txt, cloud_reliability.txt, aggregation.txt, surround.json, sizeopt.json. Seeds are fresh_seeds from base 36,200,000 (+20k/+30k/+40k/+50k offsets), with 4 threads per call. No repo file was edited. My call: the pilot world pays for one kind of computation, local evidence pooling at large body size, and evolution found it. Routing, decisions and hidden depth pay only in narrow parts of world space, and in their simple forms they create cliffs. The levers that keep everything local and still widen the niche are these: faster conduction; a family of worlds drawn per life, chosen inside a measured niche map and aggregated per life; a click that is a real decision, introduced by a curriculum; and variety inside each life through a blob-type table. A dense shaped score should be rejected, because the ledger's dense proxies predict future F worse than F itself.

working.item: SPECK (small halo, high value) is a working start world
working.evidence: 7 of 10 SPECK L4 seeds reached F >= +4 and 10 of 10 grew. In v1, 6 of 10 stayed at 1-2 cells. The first rung is visible above noise: the SPECK 2-cell clicker is +0.48 over the lone cell, against +0.04 in v1 with a per-life SD of 0.08-0.11 (RESULTS.md Pre-pilot part 10, pilot part 1).

working.item: SPECK already rewards local evidence pooling, and evolution found it (lateral computation at large size)
working.evidence: Re-measured on 256 paired lives (out/worlds_summary.txt): s5 +6.77 at 123 cells and s7 +6.54 at 95 cells. The tuned reflex knobs on a ring-4 body earn only +3.00 at the same placement range, and the untuned ring-4 reflex earns +0.80 (GS table). lateral_off removes 63-107% of F in s5-s9, with Spearman 0.71 between F and lateral share. The mechanisms are pooling: neighbour voting with an isolated event firing with p 0.04 (s4), cooperative detection with feedback inhibition (s5), and a crowding gain (s2). s4's antenna fringe is a real 2-hop lateral relay (fringe sensor -> inner sensor -> motor). So 'noisy sensors make pooling necessary' is working. What fails is only the bar of beating a reflex tuned on 57,600 lives.

working.item: Bounded growth from physics plus costs, in the better half of SPECK
working.evidence: s4-s8 stop by T/2 at 91-173 cells, through contact inhibition on n_view. Knocking out n_view sends 14 of 15 unseeded bodies to the 1,024-cell guard. Their stop sizes sit at the flat top of their own oracle-capped size curves (results.csv size_curve): s4 5.41/5.40 at caps 74/122 with 91 natural cells; s8 5.75/5.86 at 100 cells. s5 and s7 stop at 120 and 95, where their curves still rise to cap 122 (8.43, 7.71), so they stop at or near the top. No size target is hardcoded. Size also responds to the world within a life: in the 4x-background world, s2 grows 105 -> 155 cells and s7 shrinks 95 -> 87 (E1).

working.item: World rules that close cheats and control variance do their job
working.evidence: Without the timer re-placement (t_resp 0, E1), every body collapses (reflex@hollow3 8.62 -> 1.13; s5 6.77 -> 0.14) and the captures' index of dispersion rises from 1.3-1.7 to 4.4-7.9. Rule N10's timer is therefore load-bearing for both cheat resistance and selection noise. c_miss 10 makes blind pressers lose (GS6). The slit residual is unused: the largest estimated gain is +0.096 F.

working.item: Click precision evolved without any designed signal
working.evidence: E1 base: s5 and s7 capture on 49-50% of their clicks (misses 18-21 per life), against 32% for the tuned reflex@hollow3 (45 misses) and 38% for the router (out/cmiss_reprice.txt). v1 s5 evolved a 2-event centre coincidence detector (mechanisms.json).

working.item: The infrastructure for task variety already exists, so no kernel change is needed for a first family
working.evidence: build.run takes one world per life. LifeDraw shares each life's world and seed across all genomes (CRN). The envelope control already draws per-life world values keyed by (run seed, purpose, generation, life) (src/life/evaluate.py _envelope). The kernel's b2 blob has a value sign, presence probability b2_p and its own timer (b2_mode 1). I ran TWIN, DECOY-lite and nine other variants by world keys alone (worlds.py).

working.item: Critique digest items, re-scored with pilot data plus my runs
working.evidence: SUPPORTED: neuro 'a hop costs a full integration window' and simplify 'test faster conduction before the radius gene' (every evolved body gains +0.14 to +1.70 at d0 0.5; in my E1 the router's lead goes +2.17 -> +3.51; events per life are unchanged). evo 'selection cannot see differences' (E2: per-life reliability 0.026). evo 'growth that never stops is a selection-signal problem, not a missing capability' (5 of 10 stop; the growers overshoot by 0.6-0.9 F, under one parent-score SE). neuro 'hidden planes have no job in CATCH/SPECK' (inert in all 4 analysed bodies). devbio/neuro 'direction is bought through chemistry': all 4 analysed bodies build direction-specific synapses from a morphogen gradient, so that critique verdict's doubt is now refuted. WEAKENED: devbio 'morphogen escape as a size signal' and simplify 'energy store to stop growth', since growth stops on n_view alone in the best half. REFUTED IN PART: simplify 'prune a0/a1': chemistry and directional-gain knockouts cost -7 to -11 F in s5-s7. tau_tr and delta (|dF| <= 0.25) remain pruning candidates. evo 'seeded arms locked out of chemistry': supported (seeded bests 1.36-4.38 against the unseeded 6.94).

not_working.item: Routing never beats the tuned reflex (0 of 10), and the routing niche is narrow in world space, not only in body space
not_working.evidence: E1 (256 paired lives per cell, out/worlds_summary.txt): router@ring4 minus reflex@hollow3 is +2.17 +- 0.19 in base SPECK. It is about 0 or negative after any one-key world change: twin +0.37 +- 0.22, targets placed near (R 0.5-4) -0.11 +- 0.27, decoy-lite -0.09 +- 0.19, fast target (v_t 0.3) -0.48 +- 0.14, sparse receptors (lam_s 0.5) -1.28 +- 0.12. It grows with fast conduction (+3.51 +- 0.23), with 4x background noise (+1.55 +- 0.18) and with fixed placement at R 4 (+6.76, a size and placement resonance with the ring-4 rim). Sweeping the placement range (sizeopt.json, 128 lives), router@ring4 minus reflex@ring3 is -3.5 at R 1-3, +2.4 at R 2-6, +0.4 at R 3-9, and every body is at or below the lone cell at R 4-12. In body space, router knobs give 8.55 on ring 3 and 7.65 on ring 5, against 11.08 on ring 4 (SPECK_TUNE_RECORD), and the path from the best reflex dips 0.22-0.44 (GS3).
not_working.likely_cause: In a stationary world each decision is local in space and time. Routing pays only where a big body is worth having (targets at 2-6 under a sigma-0.6 halo) and only while hops are fast compared with the target's stay. Evolution reached the broad pooling optimum instead of the sharp routed one, and its per-step gradient (0.2-0.4 F) is invisible at a per-life SD of 2.0-2.5.

not_working.item: Hidden planes are inert, and they are a cost
not_working.evidence: In all four analysed bodies, hidden_off after development changes F by at most +0.04 +- 0.16; in s4 hidden cells never fire. The pilot bests still carry hidden cells: s6 has 49.3 of 173, about 0.99 F per unit of c_live; s5 14.5 (0.29); s9 13.7 (0.27) (summary/results.csv n_H).
not_working.likely_cause: This is structural in BODY-1. z >= 2 touches the world only through z = 1, so any sensory input reaching a hidden cell has already passed an act cell. Meanwhile the sense plane and the interior act cells (no open face, so they cannot pull; s5 uses them as inhibitory interneurons) are free compute inside the footprint. No reactive or short-memory task gives hidden cells a niche those cells lack.

not_working.item: Selection cannot resolve near-neutral differences, so fine improvements are drift
not_working.evidence: E2 (out/cloud_reliability.txt): the audit's 256 SPECK s5 genomes (32 parents + 224 children) on 16 fresh lives. In the 244-genome near-neutral cloud, the split-half (8 vs 8 lives) correlation of F is 0.17-0.19. That is a per-life reliability of 0.026, so 38 lives would be needed for reliability 0.5; the pilot uses 3 lives plus 4 for the shortlist. Per-life SD is 2.3-2.5, matching Poisson capture noise (R/T)*sqrt(N*ID) with N 19 and ID 1.24. The genetic SDs from split-half covariance are income 0.57, cost 0.36 and F only 0.33: the population sits on a size-economy ridge where income and cost co-vary and cancel.
not_working.likely_cause: Few, high-value, Poisson capture events (about 19 per life at 0.49 F each), and a population adapted to one fixed world, so its heritable variation lies along an iso-fitness ridge.

not_working.item: Evolved bodies are specialists to the single world they were selected in
not_working.evidence: E1 retention F(world)/F(base), averaged over the sparse, noisy, fast and decoy shifts (out/retention.txt): reflex@hollow3 0.46, reflex@ring3 0.45, router 0.36, s2 0.22, s5 0.24, s7 0.23, s4 0.16. s4's neighbour voting goes negative at 4x background (-1.23, with 162 misses per life). The more computational the body, the more fragile it is.
not_working.likely_cause: One fixed world, with nothing in selection that pays for robustness. Tuning thresholds to one background rate and one target speed is the cheapest way up.

not_working.item: Bounded growth fails in the weaker half of the SPECK seeds
not_working.evidence: s0-s3 and s9 still grow at T (101-180 cells, GB11 share growing 1.00). Each overshoots its own capped optimum by about 0.6-0.9 F: s0 4.05 at cap 122 against 3.45 at 141 cells, and s2 4.28 at cap 74 against 3.35 at about 105 cells. s9 and s3 sit roughly on a flat curve. Seeded s0 overshoots by about 3 F (4.32 at cap 74 against 1.36 at 322 cells).
not_working.likely_cause: The overgrowth penalty (0.6-0.9 F) is below one SE of a parent's 7-life selection score (about 0.75-0.95 at a per-life SD of 2.0-2.5), so this is the same noise problem as above. The capability (n_view contact inhibition) exists in every lineage. The seeded lineage is held by its seed's saturated genes.

not_working.item: In their simple forms, decision and discrimination features recreate DECOY's cliff
not_working.evidence: surround.json: a hand-built centre-surround clicker (ring 3; the interior sensors relay on ch1 to inhibit the centre sensor; 12-point grid, final 512 paired lives) beats reflex@ring3 by +1.85 +- 0.10 only in decoy2, where a decoy is always present and costs 100. There both bodies lose money (-2.67 against -4.53; the lone cell scores -0.02). In decoy-lite (p 0.5, cost 50) it loses -0.27 +- 0.09, and in base it loses -0.12 (weak inhibition) to -3.90 (strong). Re-pricing misses favours evolved click precision, but at c_miss 50 the 2-cell clicker (capture rate 0.03) falls from +0.10 to -1.64, which kills the start-small rung (cmiss_reprice.txt).
not_working.likely_cause: A fixed circuit that helps in hard situations costs in easy ones, so A2 and A1 pull against each other. Only a context-dependent (adaptive) computation can pay across a mixture, and the world never makes the situation persist long enough to make adaptation pay.

not_working.item: A dense world helps the reflex, not computation
not_working.evidence: TWIN (a second identical paying target, E1): the reflex goes 8.62 -> 14.35 and the router 10.79 -> 14.72, so the router's lead shrinks from +2.17 to +0.37. With near placement every body jumps (reflex 26.1) and the lead is 0. Captures rise only 1.38x (19.1 -> 26.4 in the s5 cloud), because travel limits the capture rate. At equal income the per-life SD therefore falls only about 15%.
not_working.likely_cause: Density shortens travel and puts a target near the rim more often, which is exactly the reflex's case. It does not create cases where an action at one site depends on other sites.

not_working.item: Apoptosis, delta and tau_tr go unused
not_working.evidence: p_die knockout is 0.00 in every body; |dF| <= 0.25 for delta and tau_tr (analysis.md knockouts).
not_working.likely_cause: The world has no damage or turnover (kill_rate is reserved), no timing or motion demand that needs delay lines, and no reward for removing cells. This is not a fault of the knobs.

proposals.title: Make conduction fast relative to the world: d0 0.5, d_min 0.25 in every CATCH/SPECK preset
proposals.change: Set the world constants d0 = 0.5 and d_min = 0.25 (keep delay_sd and jit as fractions) in catch_speck_l4/l2 and the next stage's presets. Re-tune the SPECK references at the new delay and rerun GS1-GS6, recording the change as a section-15 tweak. No organism rule changes.
proposals.targets: The payoff of multi-hop and lateral algorithms relative to the one-hop reflex (routing, pooling), without designing behaviour. It also makes the later radius-gene stage measure fan-in rather than latency.
proposals.evidence: Pilot (analysis.md): every body gains under fast conduction (router +1.99, reflex +0.99, evolved +0.14 to +1.70; s6, the most lateral-dependent body, gains +1.70). My E1 (256 paired lives, seeds 36.2M): router minus reflex@hollow3 goes +2.17 +- 0.19 -> +3.51 +- 0.23 (+62%); s5 gains +1.11 and the reflex +0.62. Kernel events per life are unchanged (1.00x for hand bodies, 0.87x for s5, which grows smaller), so the compute cost is zero. GS2 sweep: +3.32 / +2.25 / -0.56 at d0 0.5 / 1 / 2 (the 0.5 point still had d_min 0.5). Supports critique items neuro 'miscalibrated hop' and simplify 'faster conduction first'.
proposals.expressivity: Nothing is lost: delta still adds delay, so slow lines stay expressible. Deeper chains (3-4 hops) fit inside a target's stay under the body.
proposals.constraints: Local, async, no clock. A constant, not a rule. Within the user's minor-tweak permission, but it moves registered gate numbers, so record it in LIFE_ABI 15 and re-baseline. The window-scheduler tests need window_h <= d_min. Notices and claims also speed up, so re-check growth timing.
proposals.cost: Two preset values; about 1-3 CPU-hours of reference re-tuning and gates at 4 threads; one 10-seed arm (about 24 CPU-h, or about $3-8 on a rented 192-core box).
proposals.test: Pre-register a 10-seed SPECK L4 arm at d0 0.5 / d_min 0.25 against the pilot. Success if the median final F is at least the pilot's +4.91 plus 0.5, AND Spearman(F, lateral_off share) is >= 0.5, AND at least 1 seed beats the re-tuned best reflex by > 3 paired SE (the S1 routing criterion, re-based). Kill if the median falls below the pilot's.

proposals.title: Map the computation niche over world space with hand bodies before choosing any stage or family range
proposals.change: Add a scripted gate (scripts only). Run the reference set (best tuned reflex, full reflex, router or the stage's computing body, S0 champion, 2-cell clicker, lone cell) on a 3-5-level grid along each candidate world axis: sigma, lam_s, lam_bg, v_t, the R_min-R_max range, b2 twin/decoy p and value, c_miss, d0. Use 256 paired lives per cell. A stage or family may use only the region where (A1) the S0 champion and the clicker beat the lone cell and (A2) the computing body beats the best reflex by >= 3 SE.
proposals.targets: Avoids launching worlds where computation cannot pay (DECOY's cliff, TWIN's reflex bias) and chooses family ranges that keep a gradient toward routing and pooling.
proposals.evidence: My E1 and E4 show the lead is world-specific: +2.17 at base; +3.51 with fast conduction; +1.55 at 4x background; +6.76 at fixed R 4 (a size resonance); about 0 for twin, near, decoy-lite; -0.48 for fast targets; -1.28 for sparse receptors; across placement ranges -3.5 / +2.4 / +0.4 at R 1-3 / 2-6 / 3-9, with everyone below the lone cell at R 4-12. The whole E1 grid (11 worlds x 8 bodies x 256 lives) took about 15 min at 4 threads under load. Hand bodies cost 0.01-0.03 CPU-s per life.
proposals.expressivity: No change to the organism. It only prevents choosing worlds that remove the gradient toward computation.
proposals.constraints: Measurement only; nothing inside a life changes. Hand bodies remain references, never seeds.
proposals.cost: About 50 lines in scripts/life_gates.py; about 10-30 CPU-min per map.
proposals.test: For the first family run (T-family), pre-register that every axis range lies inside the mapped A1-and-A2 region. The test passes if the evolved arm's lateral_off share does not fall below the pilot's median (0.65).

proposals.title: A procedural CATCH family drawn per life (reusing the envelope machinery), with per-life percentile aggregation and a held-out box
proposals.change: Extend the envelope to task keys, or add a `task_envelope` block with the same keying (run seed, generation, life; shared by every genome, so CRN holds). Inside the niche map: sigma U[0.5,1.0], lam_s U[1,3], lam_bg log-U[0.03,0.2], v_t U[0.05,0.2], (R_min,R_max) in {(1,4),(2,6),(3,8)}, and b2 as twin or decoy-lite with b2_p U[0,0.5]. Keep base SPECK as 25-50% of lives as an anchor. Fitness = mean over a genome's lives of its percentile of F among the generation's genomes on that life. F per life stays income minus costs. Held out: a box (sigma < 0.55 and v_t > 0.17), one unseen combination (decoy + 4x background) and two extrapolations (sigma 0.4, v_t 0.3), each scored against reflex@hollow3 in the same world. The valid score stays base SPECK.
proposals.targets: The user's generalisation goal: robustness and in-life adaptation. It also exposes heritable variation that a single world hides, and lets the size bound vary by world without any size rule.
proposals.evidence: E1 retention (sparse, noisy, fast, decoy): the pilot bests keep 0.16-0.24 of their base F, against 0.45-0.46 for the hand reflex. s4 goes negative at 4x background. E2 (out/cloud_reliability.txt, aggregation.txt): for the same 244 near-neutral genomes, the genetic SD of F is 0.33 in base and 0.89 in twin; their genetic correlation across the two worlds is only 0.25. Mixing 8 base + 8 twin lives raises split-half reliability from 0.18 to 0.47-0.51. A raw mixed mean is dominated by the high-F world (r 0.90 with the twin half against 0.65 with base). The percentile costs <= 0.04 reliability within one world (0.166 against 0.180). E4: the reflex size optimum stays at ring 3 for R 1-3, 2-6 and 3-9, so the family does not destabilise the bound; R 4-12 must be excluded. Development finishes by t of about 100-512 (E1 last births; pilot GB11), so one world per life repays development once per world. Within-life variety (T-types) is cheaper per situation.
proposals.expressivity: Gains pressure for robust thresholds and adaptive gain or size, which is already expressible: s2 adapts its gain to crowding and its size 105 -> 155 cells under noise. Risk: a generalist reflex may out-select fragile computation (router retention 0.36 against reflex 0.45), which is why the ranges come from the niche map and lateral reliance is a pre-registered check.
proposals.constraints: Every world value is fixed for a whole life. Cells still sense only receptor events, so nothing new is global inside a life. The percentile is selection-level, which is allowed. Ask the user to confirm that 'task performance' now means family performance; that is a framing decision, not a rule.
proposals.cost: About 40-60 lines in src/life/evaluate.py (keys and draw) and src/evolve.py (aggregation), plus tests. Lives per generation are unchanged. Hand references per held-out cell are measured once (about 1 CPU-min). On a rented 192-core box (1,070 lives per generation at about 0.1 CPU-s) a 500-generation run takes about 1-1.5 h, the same as now.
proposals.test: Pre-register a 10-seed A/B at equal lives (family against base-only). Success if held-out-box F relative to the reflex in the same world is >= 1.5x the base arm's, base-world F is not lower by more than 1 paired SE, and the lateral_off share is >= the base arm's median minus 0.1. Also report the shortlist rank correlation (it should exceed the pilot's 0.03).

proposals.title: Keep fitness = task performance: reject distance or time-near-target shaping; add a selection-reliability readout instead
proposals.change: Do not add the ledger's dist_sum or zone_samples to F, and do not use them in pre-screening. Add two per-run readouts that cost nothing: split-half reliability of F within the recheck shortlist (its 4 recheck lives, split 2 and 2), and the captures' index of dispersion. Take information per CPU-s from allocation (racing; evo lens) and from variety (T-family). Re-price c_miss or R_cap only for economic reasons, never for noise.
proposals.targets: The denser-score question; selection noise; protecting the cost economics that set the size bound.
proposals.evidence: E2 near-neutral cloud (244 genomes x 16 lives, cloud_reliability via analyse_cloud.py). Half-life mean distance predicts F on the other half at r +0.09, and zone time at +0.09, against +0.17-0.19 for F itself. Across all genomes the figures are 0.14 and 0.49 against F's 0.77. Per life the proxies are more heritable (ICC 0.067 and 0.043 against F's 0.004), so they would be selected strongly, along traits nearly orthogonal to F, such as parking near targets (DECOY's failure mode). Misses have ICC 0.40 but r -0.02 with F. Per-life SD equals Poisson capture noise. The twin world raises captures only 1.38x, so the SD at equal income falls about 15%. A shaped term would also re-price the cell-cost trade that produced the size bound.
proposals.expressivity: Nothing changes. It avoids a proxy that would quietly redefine the task.
proposals.constraints: Matches the user's 'fitness = task performance' and the cost-based size bound. No approval needed.
proposals.cost: About 20 lines in the analysis or curves logging.
proposals.test: The readout is in place when every run row reports the shortlist split-half reliability. The decision rule is pre-registered: re-open shaping only if a proxy's cross-half correlation with F exceeds F's own on a 16-life cloud measurement in the world in use.

proposals.title: Make the hotspot a real decision through a miss-price curriculum decided by selection, not a fixed high price
proposals.change: Keep c_miss 10 in the founder phase and for small bodies. Raise it to 30 and then 50 between generations once the population median F passes thresholds set from the niche map (for example median F > 4 and median body > 14 cells). This is a selection-level curriculum, like the planned DECOY-ramp. Re-tune the A2 reference reflex at each price, so the centre sensor's coincidence threshold is fair.
proposals.targets: Computation at the hotspot: pooling evidence before clicking (a 2-hop lateral convergence onto (0,0)), and precision as a decision, while keeping the start-small rung.
proposals.evidence: Post-hoc re-pricing of 256 paired lives (behaviour does not depend on a price; cmiss_reprice.txt). Capture rate per click: s5 0.49, s7 0.50, reflex 0.32, router 0.38. Deficit against reflex@hollow3: s5 -1.85 -> -0.91 (c_miss 50) -> +0.28 +- 0.19 (c_miss 100); s7 -2.08 -> -1.02 -> +0.30 +- 0.18. The router's lead stays at about +2.15. The 2-cell clicker (capture rate 0.03) goes +0.10 -> -1.64 at c_miss 50, so a fixed high price would kill founders (GS6 history: c_miss 2 let blind pressers pay; 10 restored v1's break-even of 2/102).
proposals.expressivity: Rewards click logic built from neighbours' evidence. Nothing is removed; the start rung is kept by the ramp.
proposals.constraints: A price only, and no cell reads it. The ramp is decided outside lives (allowed). It shifts the cost economics slowly, so report size against capped optimum at each step. Approval: a minor tweak, but tell the user, because it changes the reward schedule.
proposals.cost: About 30 lines in evolve.py (ramp keyed on the curves); reflex re-tune at 2 prices (about 1-2 CPU-h).
proposals.test: Pre-register for 10 seeds: the final bests' click capture rate is > 0.6. The deficit against the reflex re-tuned at the final price is smaller than the pilot's at c_miss 10 (median -2.0). P.chains on hotspot clicks shows >= 30% of click-causing chains passing through a lateral hop (they are near 0 in the hand reflex).

proposals.title: Replace b2's seven special keys with a blob-type table, per-placement type draws, and Poisson world 'epochs' for variety within a life
proposals.change: World-side kernel change only. Each life gets a small table of K <= 4 blob types (sigma, brightness lam_s, v_t, value, rho, presence). Each placement draws a type from the life's current mixture. At Poisson world times (mean 200-300) the mixture is redrawn: an epoch, for example a decoy-rich phase, a dim-target phase or a fast-target phase. Types differ only in features the cells sense (width, event rate, speed). Value switches between sensed-identical types are excluded until a local consequence signal (taste) is approved. TWIN, DECOY and DECOY-ramp become rows of the table, and b2_amp/sigma/value/rho/p/mode are retired.
proposals.targets: Variety within one life (amortises development), rule switches within a life on sensed statistics, adaptive and context-dependent computation, and a cleaner rule set.
proposals.evidence: The b2 machinery works (twin and decoy measured in E1). Decoy-lite (p 0.5, cost 50, sigma 1.5) keeps reflex@hollow3 at 5.68, 66% of base, so A1 holds where full DECOY failed. surround.json shows why fixed computations fail across a mixture: a centre-surround clicker gains +1.85 +- 0.10 only when decoys are always present (both bodies below the lone cell) and loses -0.27 +- 0.09 in decoy-lite. A body that switches surround inhibition on during decoy-rich epochs would collect the gain without paying the base-world cost (-0.12 to -3.90), and that needs persistence, which epochs provide. Evolved bodies already adapt cell state over tens to about 100 units (s2's crowding gain), on the same timescale as a 200-300-unit epoch. Development is done by t of about 100-512, so 3-5 epochs per life cost no extra development.
proposals.expressivity: Gains decoys, twins, dim or fast phases and their mixtures in one mechanism. Loses nothing that b2 could express (b2 is the K = 2 case).
proposals.constraints: Only the world changes, and cells see only receptor events. No clock or global channel is added to the organism, and the world already has Poisson timers. The kernel and ABI change needs the user's sign-off as a world-rule replacement. A value-switch variant needs the taste signal and the user's approval.
proposals.cost: About 150-250 kernel lines (place, halo and thinning bound per type, accountant) plus spec/reference, tests and gates; no organism or genome change. Thinning: compute lam_max per type to avoid more rejected receptor candidates (already 54% of events).
proposals.test: Pre-register for 10 seeds in an epoch world chosen from the niche map: (1) the S0 champion and the clicker earn above the lone cell; (2) the evolved arm beats a base-only arm on held-out epoch lives by > 3 SE; (3) a genes_blind fork from T/2 costs > 25% of second-half income there, against < 10% in base, which shows in-life adaptation is in use.

proposals.title: Stop scoring hidden-plane use as a goal in BODY-1 reactive stages; run them at L_max 2 (user decision)
proposals.change: For S1-type stages (SPECK, the family, click decision), use the catch_speck_l2 preset, or add an L2 arm, and drop 'hidden cells in use' from the success language. Bring back L_max 4 at a stage where hidden_off is required to cost >= 30% (the stage table's S2 rule), and only after a hand body shows a hidden circuit beating its in-plane twin.
proposals.targets: Clean criteria (computation is measured by multi-hop chains and lateral reliance, not by plane occupancy), cell economy, and compute.
proposals.evidence: Hidden cells are inert in all four analysed bodies (hidden_off after development <= +0.04 +- 0.16; they never fire in s4). Upkeep: s6 carries 49.3 hidden cells (about 0.99 F per unit at c_live 0.02), s5 14.5 (0.29), s9 13.7 (0.27). The cause is structural: z >= 2 reaches the world only through z = 1, while z = 0 and interior z = 1 cells are free compute (s5's interior act cells are its inhibitory interneurons). The pilot's v1 L2 against L4 comparison was too small to say anything (1 of 3 against 4 of 10). Supports the critique's neuro item (partly p3).
proposals.expressivity: Hidden-plane memory and isolation from receptor noise are lost for now, and nothing used in the pilot. They can be restored when a task needs them.
proposals.constraints: L_max 4 is the user's design (spec.py comment; rule N2), so this needs the user's approval. Locality and the clock are untouched.
proposals.cost: Config only. Compute per life falls by the hidden share (0-28% of cells in the SPECK bests).
proposals.test: Pre-register a 10-seed SPECK L2 arm against the pilot's L4: median final F >= L4's; lateral_off share not lower; CPU per generation lower. If L2 is worse by > 1 SE in median F, keep L4.

proposals.title: Temporal tasks (LEAD, BLINK) only behind a hand-built computing reference, and value switches only with a local taste signal
proposals.change: Before any motion-prediction or occlusion stage: build a hand interceptor (a Reichardt-style delay-line pair using delta) and a direction-memory body, and require each to pass A1-A4 on the niche map. Value switches within a life (a type that was food becomes poison) wait for the neuro critique's local taste event plus per-contact plasticity, under the user's approval.
proposals.targets: Prediction of motion, memory of a vanished target, and adaptation to new rules, without launching worlds that only make everything worse.
proposals.evidence: E1 fast target (v_t 0.3): retention is reflex 0.38, router 0.26, evolved 0.08-0.18, and the router loses to the reflex (-0.48 +- 0.14). No existing circuit gains from motion, so LEAD as a bare world switch is a cliff. The prior prototype study measured occlusion at +0.05, matched by a single-cell slow state (BODY_DESIGN_PROPOSAL S2 row), so BLINK alone does not force network computation. delta and tau_tr are unused today (|dF| <= 0.25); a timing task is what would exercise them.
proposals.expressivity: Adds interception and occlusion worlds (a world-side visibility timer for BLINK), and later adds learning from consequences.
proposals.constraints: BLINK needs a world-side visibility timer (a world rule, no organism change). Taste adds a fixed local sense rule tied to the hotspot, so it needs the user's approval. STDP is an organism change (ABI bump).
proposals.cost: Hand interceptor and gates: about 1-2 days. BLINK world timer: about 50 kernel lines. Taste plus STDP: the critique's largest item.
proposals.test: Launch a temporal stage only if its hand computing body beats the best re-tuned reflex by >= 3 SE and its matching fork (lateral_off, or genes_blind for memory) removes >= 50% of the gain, with the S0 champion still above the lone cell.

assessed.lens: Cell rules, cleanliness and expressivity. Which fixed rules and knobs earned their keep, which are workarounds, and how to get a smaller, cleaner rule set without losing expressivity. Includes the gene clock against spike timing, and receptor thinning. New experiments: scripts and outputs in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-jgon-project-ml-cell-dev/aefb0c66-3af5-49c4-936c-154d6434706c/scratchpad/review/rules/. xrules.py runs reference-simulator arms (summary in arms_table.tsv). p0scan.py runs kernel scans (p0scan.jsonl, p0scan_model.txt). shat_probe.py logs the direction term (shat_s5.json). Every life seed is fresh_seeds(n, seed0=36,300,000). The noop arm equals the kernel bitwise in 4 of 4 lives.

working.item: The LIF cell core is expressive enough for evolved local computation, and the bodies use per-slot weights heavily. The core is: threshold 1, rest set by the genes (b), tau_m, refractory period, and weights the receiver signs per channel on the q8 grid.
working.evidence: Three lineages evolved computations beyond the column reflex. s4: a weighted 2-vote sensor fires with P 0.04 on one own event and 0.82-0.87 on one event plus one neighbour spike. s5: coincidence windows of 4.6-5.5 units, plus act-to-sensor feedback inhibition (blocking the downward messages costs -5.61 +- 0.38). s2: gain set by crowding (mechanisms.json). New: making every slot's weights equal per channel after t=256 (iso arm) costs s5 -10.10 +- 0.41 (captures 15.3 to 0.03, n 32). Direction-specific weights are load-bearing.

working.item: Reset to v=0 above a negative rest acts as an afterdepolarisation, and evolution exploits it. Keep it with no knob.
working.evidence: s4: after a spike a sensor restarts at 0 against a rest of -1.7, so for about 1.8 units one event re-fires it. Removing this costs -0.90 +- 0.30, or about 1.4 F in the verifier's run. s5's sensors are primed the same way (P re-fire 0.75), and the cell's own feedback inhibition cancels the priming. One fixed constant gives a short-term memory for free. It is a feature, not an ABI accident: document it as such in section 15.

working.item: The contact-count input n_view is the universal growth brake, a cheap in-life sensor, and enough for bounded growth in the best bodies.
working.evidence: Knocking out n_view sends 14 of 15 unseeded grown bodies to the 1,024 guard (dF -16.5 to -28.0). In s2, gain adaptation after a neighbour dies is causal through n_view and disappears when n_view is held fixed. The five best SPECK bodies (s4-s8) stop growing within their life (share still growing 0.00-0.02), with no size target and no morphogen leak or energy store. This weakens the premise of critique devbio-p1 (morphogen escape) and simplify-p1 (energy store) that 'growth never stops'; 5 of 10 SPECK bodies still grow.

working.item: Development rules (plane cues is_S/is_M, zeta, the asym x Q division split) build sensor/motor columns reliably.
working.evidence: in_planes knockout: -1.4 to -9.1. zeta knockout: up to -18.5, with growth running away. asym knockout: -21 to -24 and the guard in the v1 and seeded arms. Act cells bud straight up: 96% in s4, and 33-50 vertical against 4-8 in-plane divisions in s5. Every body regrew the column reflex.

working.item: Value-less spike channels work as transmitter labels. That is a clock-robust route to vertical wiring.
working.evidence: s4 sends ch0 from sense cells only and ch1 from act cells only. Averaging each cell's weights per channel over all its slots (iso) therefore costs s4 only -1.12 +- 0.55 (n 24), against -10.10 in s5, which wires vertically through chemistry. Slowing s4's gene/chemistry clock 4x after t=512 costs -0.04 +- 0.42. Removing emission on channel 1 costs -11.7 (s5), -7.0 (s9) and -6.3 (s8).

working.item: Hop latency is a real, selectable cost, so the time constants matter.
working.evidence: Faster conduction (d0 0.5, d_min 0.25) helps every body in the analysis: +0.14 to +1.70 on 256 lives. The router gains +1.99 against the reflex's +0.99, so the router's margin grows by about 1.0. My kernel scan (64 lives, seed0 36.3M): +0.60 to +1.31 for s5, s4, s2, s7 and v1 s5.

not_working.item: Direction-specific synapses can only be built through morphogen chemistry (or by spending the channel labels). That is a fragile, costly, clock-dependent workaround for 'listen to the cell below, not beside'.
not_working.evidence: All four analysed bodies read direction from a standing morphogen gradient. New (reference, freeze at fork): replacing each cell's weights with its per-face averages (in-plane, up, down, per channel) keeps F: s5 -0.24 +- 0.66 (n 32), s2 -0.14 +- 0.67 (n 24), v1 s5 -0.13 +- 0.19 (n 24), s4 -0.78 +- 0.64 (n 32, the only body with real planar anisotropy: the SD of in-plane w0 within a cell is 0.31, against 0.08-0.11 in the others). Removing direction entirely costs s5 -10.10. So almost all of the information this chemistry carries is 3 face numbers per cell. The costs: secretion is 0.29 of s5's 2.98 cost per unit time; pol also steers division placement; v1 s5's secretion swap flips the signs; s5 and v1 s5 spend both channels as excitatory/inhibitory halves to get 3 signs out of w(1+a*shat), with ch0 clipped at +2.0.
not_working.likely_cause: w_eff depends on the slot only through shat_d (kernel.c derive), even though the kernel already tells vertical faces apart for zeta (rule N8, off_z). No local primitive gives per-face gain, so evolution builds one from plane-specific secretion plus max-normalisation, with shat = +-1 on the vertical slot.

not_working.item: Wiring built from chemistry is calibrated to the tick period: the direction term carries a tick-phase artefact.
not_working.evidence: s5, with the gene/chemistry clock slowed after t=256 (membrane untouched): x4 -10.25 +- 0.55 (captures 17.1 to 2.6, misses 15 to 30); x2 -4.02 +- 0.68. With the phenotype fixed in both arms, x4 still costs -9.64 +- 0.62. With weights held and only the genes slowed it costs -1.44 +- 0.55, so the damage runs through chemistry into the weights. The shat probe shows the mechanism: the mean in-plane shat in the sense plane rises from +0.04 to +0.19 at x4, so the net lateral weight rises from +0.33 to +0.59 (inhibitory w1 -0.82 to -0.65). This breaks the near-cancellation between the excitatory and inhibitory channels and the sense sheet runs away. Vertical shat stays at about +-0.95. The critique (devbio 4a) predicted this artefact: a neighbour's post-secretion concentration is compared with the cell's own pre-secretion level.
not_working.likely_cause: In the s_d formula, inc (the neighbour's concentration just after secreting sec*dt) is compared with the cell's own m at a different phase. The difference grows with the tick interval, and max-normalisation amplifies it. Bodies that route vertically through channel labels (s4) or that tolerate it (v1 s5: -0.18 +- 0.13) survive.

not_working.item: Gene clock and spikes run on the same time scale. Ticks dominate CPU, and after development the gene network churns without effect.
not_working.evidence: P0 2 against hop d0 1 and tau_m 2-4 in the evolved sensors. The fastest gene class has tau of about 2.9 units. Ticks are 68-74% of modelled CPU (audit model: 187 ns per heap event + 1.9 us per tick, applied to p0scan counts). In s5 the knobs change 60-86 times per cell after t=256, yet pheno_fixed costs -0.04 +- 0.18, and s4 freeze at 512 gives +0.27 +- 0.18. A 4x slower clock after development is harmless in s4 and v1 s5. It costs s2 -1.47 +- 0.62, but only because growth slows (108 to 79 cells; its relay pays only above about 70 cells). Whole-life P0 4 on unchanged genomes costs -0.57 to -2.97 while halving ticks (s5: 59k to 26k).
not_working.likely_cause: Gene relaxation (lambda) and the fate probabilities p_div/p_die are defined per tick, not per unit time. Development speed and chemistry are therefore tied to the tick count, so the clock period is not a free numerical step, and nothing lets a mature cell tick slowly.

not_working.item: Knobs and inputs that never earned their keep: delta, tau_tr, chi (mostly), phi (mostly), and the rho input. p_die is a required rule but is unused.
not_working.evidence: Knockouts on all 21 final bests (256 paired lives each): delta |dF| <= 0.13; tau_tr <= 0.25; rho input <= 0.19; p_die 0.00 everywhere, with 0 deaths per life. chi matters in 2 of 21 (-1.97, -0.97) and phi in 1 of 21 (-1.40). These 5 readout rows are 45 of the 207 mutable readout entries, about 22%. chi drifts the division direction when it moves. This supports critique simplify-p3 for delta, tau_tr and chi, and refutes it for a0/a1 (-8.5 to -10.0 in s5-s7) and asym (growth runs away).
not_working.likely_cause: The tasks are purely reactive. The genes read traces only at ticks and already low-pass them through their own rate classes, so tau_tr is redundant. delta can only slow conduction, which hurts every body. Nothing in these tasks rewards removing a cell: a death forfeits c_div, there are no wounds, and a hollow sense plane can be grown. The p_die prior also sits at -2.

not_working.item: Hidden planes are inert and cost about 4% of F.
not_working.evidence: hidden_off after development: s5 +0.04 +- 0.16; s4 0.000 exactly (hidden cells never fire); s2 +0.01 +- 0.11; v1 s5 +0.001 +- 0.008. s5 carries 15 hidden cells, about 0.29 F of living cost out of 6.8. This supports critique neuro-p2 (drop them until needed) and evo-p3.
not_working.likely_cause: SPECK is reactive: the reflex and the ring-4 router never need depth. A hidden cell reaches the screen only through act cells. Without a face gain, a vertical relay needs the chemical wiring above, so depth has no use in this task and is also hard to wire. z=2 and z=3 get identical cues.

not_working.item: Receptor thinning wastes about half of all scheduled events.
not_working.evidence: Receptor candidates are 54% of heap events, with 4.1-4.4% accepted in SPECK (audit). p0scan: 70k-113k candidates per life against about 3-5k accepted events.
not_working.likely_cause: One global bound, lam_max = lam_bg + lam_s = 2.05 per sense cell per unit, is applied to every sense cell regardless of its distance from the target (sigma 0.6), and the background and halo processes are thinned together.

proposals.title: Receiver face gains: per-cell k_down, k_lat, k_up multiplying the existing weight law
proposals.change: ABI 4: w_eff[d][c] = q8(w_c * k_face(d) * (1 + a_c * shat_d)), with face(d) from off_z (in-plane, up, down). Three new readout knobs, each decoded with q8 (signed, [-2, 2]). The founder prior is exactly 1 (a0 = 1, A row starting at 0 but mutable), so a padded ABI-3 genome lives bitwise as before. Keep two channels, a_c, pol and the chemistry unchanged for planar direction. When the radius gene lands, add k_lat2 (the second ring) in the same table.
proposals.targets: Direction-specific synapses without chemistry. Frees ch1 from excitatory/inhibitory duty so it can be a real label. Makes column relays, feedback inhibition and hidden-plane relays (k_up on act cells) one- or two-mutation features instead of coordinated secretion + pol + a + emission patterns. Removes the clock fragility of vertical wiring. Supports routing: a relay needs lateral input weak and vertical input strong, which k_lat sets directly.
proposals.evidence: Per-face averages of post-development weights keep F in all 4 bodies tested (s5 -0.24 +- 0.66, s2 -0.14 +- 0.67, v1 s5 -0.13 +- 0.19, s4 -0.78 +- 0.64), while isotropic weights cost s5 -10.10 +- 0.41. So the face table expresses about 90-100% of what chemistry built. Chemistry-built wiring breaks under a 2x/4x clock (-4.02 / -10.25 in s5) through the shat artefact (lateral shat +0.04 to +0.19). The channel-label route (s4) is robust, but it consumes both channels. Secretion is 0.29 of s5's 2.98 cost per unit time. Critique digest: neuro-p1 (apical-basal polarity) and evo-p3 (vertical gain) are now strongly supported. The verifier's 'evidence does not hold up' (devbio-p1 polarity) is overturned by the post-hoc mechanisms and these arms. Inherited division-axis polarity (devbio-p1) is the alternative for the PLANAR part only: it would fail for the 4-8 act cells per life born in-plane, and the vertical axis is already local knowledge (N8).
proposals.expressivity: Gained: an independent magnitude and sign per face with one channel (for example from below +2.5, lateral +0.3, from above -1.4, as s5 needs); lateral silence with strong vertical input; excitatory relays in both directions; hidden relays. Lost: nothing (k = 1 is ABI 3 exactly). Planar or radial direction (s4's fringe, worth at most about 1 F) still comes from chemistry.
proposals.constraints: Local: the receiver uses only which of its own faces an arrival came through, a distinction the kernel already makes (zeta, rule N8). No clock, no global channel, no designed behaviour: evolution sets k per cell through its genes. It changes the synapse rule and needs an ABI bump, so it should go to the user as a short section-15 entry with this evidence. It is arguably within the user's minor-tweak latitude, but I would confirm, and bundle it with the radius gene's ABI 4 as the critique advised.
proposals.cost: About 30-50 kernel lines (decode, derive) plus the reference.py mirror, pad, knob table, bitwise tests at k = 1 and a founder census (about 32k lives). 3 readout rows (+51 genome floats, or +17 net with R-prune). Runtime about 0. Test: one 10-seed SPECK L4 arm of 500 generations against the current control, about 240 CPU-h (about $15-20 spot on a 192-core box).
proposals.test: Pre-registered against a same-budget ABI-3 control (10 seeds each, SPECK L4). (1) Median final F of the face arm >= control + 0.5, or within 0.5 with secretion cost per unit time at least 30% lower. (2) In at least 5 of the face-arm bests, a k_face knockout costs at least 50% of F, i.e. evolution uses the primitive. (3) The share of rim-motor chains with a receptor origin in another column (probe chain_summary rec_other_col) has a median >= control. (4) Stretch: at least 1 of 10 bodies beats reflex@hollow3 by > 3 SE. With k = 1, golden hashes are unchanged.

proposals.title: Freeze the null knobs now (tau_tr, chi, delta) and drop tau_tr and chi at ABI 4. Keep p_die, phi and rho
proposals.change: Harness: add a `frozen_knobs` list to the genome config. The A row is set to 0 and a0 to the neutral code, and mutation skips them: tau_tr at 8, chi at 0, delta at 0. This is a mutation mask in LifeLayout.mutate, with no ABI change. ABI 4: remove the tau_tr row (trace time constant fixed at 8, the knockout value) and the chi row (reserve a dedicated knob if rotation is built). Keep the delta row frozen until a temporal task (LEAD/BLINK) arrives, then reintroduce it as a signed conduction knob with a fast level priced per spike. Keep p_die (a user requirement), phi (s8 -1.40) and the rho input (cheap, and the only sensory-history input for future adaptation tasks).
proposals.targets: A minimal rule set and less pleiotropic drift: chi rotates division placement when it drifts. A smaller contract and readout: the readout line is the hottest tick line, 7% of CPU.
proposals.evidence: Knockouts on all 21 final bests: delta |dF| <= 0.13, tau_tr <= 0.25, chi matters in 2 of 21 (-1.97, -0.97), and both lineages used it as one of several shape knobs. The genes sample traces only at ticks (every about 2 units) and filter them through their own rate classes, so tau_tr's window choice is redundant. delta can only slow conduction, while faster conduction helps every body (+0.14 to +1.70). Freezing removes 27 of the 207 mutable readout entries (13%), about 6% of all point mutations. Critique simplify-p3 is supported for these three and refuted for a0/a1 and asym.
proposals.expressivity: Lost: a per-cell trace window (redundant with gene rate classes), chiral division placement (no current or planned task uses it, apart from future rotation, which needs its own knob anyway), and slower-than-contact delays (kept frozen, not deleted, until a temporal task). Nothing used by any of the 21 bests is lost.
proposals.constraints: Only removes fixed rules and knobs. No new channel or clock. A minor tweak under the user's standing latitude. The ABI-4 removal is bundled with R-face-gains, so knob count goes 23 -> 24, or 23 once delta is dropped.
proposals.cost: Freeze: about 20 lines in src/genome.py plus a test, and a founder census. Removal: a few lines in decode, spec and the ABI doc inside the ABI-4 bump. No extra evaluation compute.
proposals.test: Founder census with the freeze: earner rate within +-20% of the current census, and extinct share within +-3 points. In the next matrix, the frozen arm's median final F is no worse than control - 0.5. Because the knockouts are already null, a separate A/B is optional.

proposals.title: Set d0 0.5 and d_min 0.25 for the next stage (world constants)
proposals.change: World presets for the next SPECK or S1 matrix: d0 0.5, d_min 0.25 (delay_sd and jit stay fractions). Re-tune the hand reflex and router there and rerun GS1-GS6. The window scheduler needs window_h <= d_min.
proposals.targets: Makes routing and multi-hop computation pay more (the router's margin grows by about 1 F). Separates time scales: a hop becomes about tau_m/8 to tau_m/4.
proposals.evidence: Pilot: fast conduction helps every one of 21 bodies (+0.14 to +1.70) and the router more than the reflex (+1.99 against +0.99). Mine: +0.60 to +1.31 on 64 lives for s5, s4, s2, s7 and v1 s5. Modelled CPU per life is unchanged (0.97-1.13x). Supports critique neuro-p2 and simplify-p2.
proposals.expressivity: Gained: deeper relay chains fit in the sensorimotor loop. Lost: nothing.
proposals.constraints: World physics only. Local and asynchronous, no clock, no designed behaviour. A minor tweak. d_min also shortens notices, claims and packets (a newborn knows its neighbours at 2 d_min), so re-check growth timing.
proposals.cost: A preset change, plus a few CPU-hours of gate re-tuning on the laptop.
proposals.test: GS2 rerun: the router's lead over the best tuned reflex at d0 0.5 / d_min 0.25 is >= +3.0 F (n 1024) and lateral_off removes >= 50% of it. In the next pilot, the share of seeds whose best has lateral_off removing >= 50% of F is >= the d0-1 pilot's (5 of 10).

proposals.title: Make gene and fate rates per unit time, compare like with like in the direction term, then slow the gene clock (P0 4)
proposals.change: ABI 4: (a) gene relaxation g <- s + (g - s) * exp(-dt / tau_k), with the 7 rate classes decoded as time constants (about 2.9-255 units, today's values at P0 2). (b) Fates p = 1 - exp(-h * dt), with h = today's per-tick value / 2. (c) s_d = sum_i pol_i * (inc[d][i] - c_self[i]), where c_self is the cell's own concentration at its last shipment (same phase as the neighbour's conc). A contact with no packet yet gets s_d = 0. Keep max-normalisation for now: s4's planar fringe relies on it. (d) decode_dm's P_MAX becomes 1.5*P0, so the shipping clamp does not move with the clock. Then, as a world setting, P0 = 4. Later and optional: a per-cell tick-period knob {x1, x2, x4} with a small per-tick price, so evolution chooses its own time-scale separation. That later step needs approval, because it adds a price.
proposals.targets: Time-scale separation between genes and spikes. The single biggest exact compute lever on the cell side. Removes a hidden dependence of development, chemistry and wiring on tick count and phase.
proposals.evidence: Ticks are 68-74% of modelled CPU. P0 4 halves ticks and gives a modelled 1.8-2.0x per life for same-size bodies (s5 0.152 to 0.085, s4 0.102 to 0.050, s7 0.123 to 0.061 CPU-s). After development a 4x slower clock is harmless for s4 (-0.04 +- 0.42) and v1 s5 (-0.18 +- 0.13), and s2's loss (-1.47) comes from slower growth (108 to 79 cells). s5's collapse (-10.25, x2 -4.02) comes from the phase artefact in shat (lateral +0.04 to +0.19), which (c) removes. Genes alone, with weights held, cost -1.44 +- 0.55. pheno_fixed after development costs about 0 in s5 and s4, though knobs flip 60-86 times per cell. Whole-life P0 4 on unchanged genomes costs -0.57 to -2.97, which shows the laws are per tick, not that slow genes are worse. Supports critique devbio-4a (like with like) and refines neuro-p3: max-normalisation is useful, and the phase artefact is the noise.
proposals.expressivity: Lost: gene responses faster than the tick period (at P0 4, about 4-8 units; s2's enclosure response takes about 7 units, which is borderline). Gained: P0 becomes a pure accuracy/compute knob, so future tasks can choose it, and planar chemical direction becomes reliable.
proposals.constraints: The clock stays per-cell, jittered and asynchronous. No central clock, no global channel, no designed schedule. It replaces per-tick laws with per-time laws, which is cleaner. A minor tweak by the user's standard, but it changes every life: do it at a stage boundary, in the same ABI 4 as R-face-gains, and rerun the gates. Max division rate becomes 1 per 4 units, so check the development speed of the hand GRN grower (GS5).
proposals.cost: About 40 kernel lines plus the reference mirror and tests (the per-time gene law, fate hazard, the c_self field, the dm decode). Test compute: one 5-seed SPECK pair at 500 generations (about 120 CPU-h for control; the new arm about half).
proposals.test: (1) CPU per generation at P0 4 <= 0.6x the P0-2 control at matched body size. (2) Median final F >= control - 0.5 (5 seeds each, same lives budget). (3) Hand GS5 GRN grower within 0.5 F of its P0-2 score. (4) With (c), the slowed-clock fork x4 after development on the new bests costs |dF| < 1 in at least 4 of 5 bodies.

proposals.title: Sample receptor events as background plus halo, thinning only the halo under a local bound
proposals.change: Implementation, not a rule: the receptor rule (Poisson at lam_bg + lam_s*halo(dist)) is unchanged. First, the audit's bitwise-exact early rejection: take the acceptance draw first and skip the exp calls for far cells. Then, distribution-exact: sample background events directly at lam_bg, and halo candidates at a per-cell bound lam_s*halo(d_lb), where d_lb is a lower bound on the cell-target distance over a short window (from the maximum speeds of dot and target).
proposals.targets: Compute: about half of all heap events.
