proposals.evidence: Candidates are 54% of heap events with 4.1-4.4% accepted (audit). p0scan: 70k-113k candidates per life against a few thousand accepted.
proposals.expressivity: Unchanged: the same stochastic process.
proposals.constraints: No change to the organism or the world law, so no approval needed. The second step changes random streams (not bitwise), so goldens must be regenerated and done between experiments.
proposals.cost: Step 1: small, bitwise-exact. Step 2: medium (about 80 kernel lines plus the reference). Modelled saving: about 10-15% of CPU now and about 25% after P0 4.
proposals.test: A KS test on accepted-event inter-arrival times per sense cell (p > 0.05 over 256 lives). Mean F of the hand reflex and router on 1024 lives within 1 SE of the current implementation. Heap events per life down >= 40%.

proposals.title: Run reactive-stage arms at L_max 2; bring hidden planes back when a task needs memory, wired with k_up
proposals.change: Config: the next S1-type and radius-gene matrix uses catch_speck_l2 (or keeps one L4 arm for comparison). Add no hidden-plane cues now; once face gains exist, a hidden relay is a k_up/k_down setting on act and hidden cells. Restore L_max 4 with the first task where hidden_off must cost >= 30% (stage table).
proposals.targets: Removes about 4% dead-weight cost and search space in tasks that cannot use depth. Keeps depth as a ready capability for memory tasks.
proposals.evidence: hidden_off after development is null in all four bodies (s5 +0.04 +- 0.16, s4 exactly 0, s2 +0.01 +- 0.11, v1 s5 +0.001 +- 0.008). s5 carries 15 hidden cells, about 0.29 F. Supports critique neuro-p2. v1 L2 against L4 (1 of 3 against 4 of 10 growing) is too small to say anything.
proposals.expressivity: Lost in reactive tasks: nothing measurable. Retained for later stages.
proposals.constraints: L_max 4 is the user's own design choice (spec.py comment), so this needs the user's decision. It touches no locality or clock rule.
proposals.cost: Config only. The compute is one arm.
proposals.test: In a speck_l2 arm against speck_l4 (10 seeds each), the L2 median final F >= the L4 median - 0.3, and growth onset is no later. If L2 is worse by > 0.5, keep L4.

proposals.title: Later, with a damage or regrowth task: merge p_div and p_die into one signed fate knob
proposals.change: ABI 5 (or a later bump): a single readout y_fate. y > +0.125 gives division hazard 2^(k-8), |y| <= 0.125 means quiescent, and y < -0.125 gives an apoptosis hazard 2^(k-8). The founder prior is centred in the division band as now. This removes one readout row, and death becomes the next step past the quiescence that the n_view brake already produces.
proposals.targets: Makes genome-driven death reachable where a task rewards it, such as wounds (bell_v2 kill_rate) or remodelling, with fewer rules.
proposals.evidence: p_die knockout is 0.00 in all 21 bests and there are 0 deaths per life. Evolved bests drifted p_die's offset to -0.56 to -2.6 and still never use it (critique evo-p3). The brake (n_view) already pushes fate toward 0 in every lineage.
proposals.expressivity: Lost: a cell that both divides and dies stochastically (turnover inside a dividing cell). Gained: death is one step from quiescence instead of an independent switch held off at -2.
proposals.constraints: Touches the user's genome-driven death requirement, so it needs approval. It is still local and genome-driven. There is a risk of extinction spirals, which needs a census.
proposals.cost: Small kernel/decode change plus a census of about 32k lives. Only worth testing alongside a task where death can pay.
proposals.test: Founder census: extinct share <= control + 5 points. In a wound world, the fraction of bests with p_die-equivalent knockout |dF| > 0.5 is >= 30%, against 0% now.

assessed.lens: Development and morphology (D). New experiments are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-jgon-project-ml-cell-dev/aefb0c66-3af5-49c4-936c-154d6434706c/scratchpad/review/dev/ (scripts e1-e10 with their .json/.log outputs). All use kernel lives on the 10 SPECK L4 bests (plus a few v1 and seeded bodies), seeds fresh_seeds(n, 36.40M-36.46M), threads 4. E1 forks division_off at 64-768 under each T in {768, 1024, 1536}, n 768. E2/E7/E8 read 16 kernel fate logs per body. E4 runs hidden_off at 256 (frozen) and regrows each genome with no hidden planes (catch_speck_l2), n 512. E5 kills 25% of cells at t 40/80/150/600, n 256. E10 compares first-half and second-half F, n 512.

working.item: Contact inhibition through the contact count (n_view) evolved in every lineage that grew
working.evidence: Pilot part 3: with n_view knocked out, 14 of 15 unseeded grown bodies run to the 1,024-cell guard. In the SPECK bests, the genes that drive p_div weight n_view at |2.6-23.7|, for example s1 g7 -23.7, s6 g7 -19.1 and s8 g5 -13.8 (e6_genome_growth.log). Caveat: the founder prior gives n_view a W std of 8, against 0.5-2 for every other input (configs/life_catch.yaml input_init). The brake is favoured by the prior, but it is not a fixed rule.

working.item: Bounded growth emerged without any size rule in the 5 best SPECK lineages: they grow in a burst, then stop
working.evidence: Cells at t=64: s5 110, s6 138, s7 93, s8 72 (s4 22). Share of final size reached by t=256: 0.95-1.00 (s4 0.71). Births after t=512: 0-3 per life (e2_anatomy). For s4, stopping growth anywhere from 256 to 768 changes F by only +0.01 to +0.03 (e1_b.log). These five are the five highest-F bodies.

working.item: Physics plus costs do give an interior size optimum for competent circuits
working.evidence: Hand reflex: ring 2 +5.01, ring 3 +5.06. GS3 routers at ring 5 and ring 6 score 7.2 and 13.8 F below ring 4. The stoppers' oracle-capped size curves still rise up to 74-122 cells (s5 5.47 -> 8.43, s7 6.36 -> 7.71; results.csv size_curve), and they end at 91-173 cells, close to that range.

working.item: Lineage builds the reflex wire: each column is a mother-daughter pair
working.evidence: In 9 of 10 SPECK bests, 90-100% of act cells are daughters of the sense cell directly below (e2_anatomy act_from_below). The one vertical contact between them is the reflex arc, so the wiring comes from division geometry and no role is designed. s6 is the exception: 58% of its act cells come from in-plane act divisions, and it is the only body with 0 holes in the act plane.

working.item: Developmental by-products get recruited into computation
working.evidence: s4: the sense disk outgrows the motor disk, leaving about 20 motor-less fringe sensors. They became an inward antenna (+1.6-1.9 inward, about 0 outward); silencing them costs -1.42 ± 0.42 F. s5: the interior act cells, which the body needs anyway as filler, became the sense sheet's inhibitory interneurons; the downward-feedback lesion costs -5.6 (mechanisms.json). Division of labour emerged from the shape of growth.

working.item: Interior act cells are physically necessary and nearly free, so cost and physics should stay as they are
working.evidence: A stroke pulls along the sum of the cell's open in-plane faces (kernel.c catch_stroke). Without an interior, a rim cell's inner face pulls it inward: 'an act ring's inner rim pulls toward the hole', and the hand-tuned best reflex keeps a full act disk under a hollow sense plane. All interior act cells of a SPECK best together fire 0.2-0.96 spikes per unit (e2_anatomy). At about 0.016 per spike (spike + twitch + 8 messages) that is <= 0.015 F/unit, under 0.3% of F. Their real cost is living, 0.15-0.66 F/unit, and that buys the outward-facing rim. My call: no change.

not_working.item: Half the lineages develop slowly, and that, more than failing to stop, is their growth problem
not_working.evidence: Growers s0, s1, s2, s3, s9 have 3-14 cells at t=64 (stoppers 22-138) and reach only 13-44% of their final size by t=256. Across the 10 SPECK bests, F rank-correlates with early size (cells at t=64/128/256: rho +0.94/+0.95/+0.96, permutation p < 0.001) and not with final size (rho +0.13). Stopping growers at t=256 costs -0.40 to -1.76 F (e1). Their first-half F is 1.6-3.9 against a second-half F of 3.8-5.2. The second-minus-first gap is 1.3-3.1 for growers and 0.8-1.7 for stoppers (e10). Timing explains about 0.5 of the 2.5 F grower-stopper gap; the rest is circuit quality at maturity.
not_working.likely_cause: Each lineage locks in its developmental mode early. Growers coalesced to one breed at generation 2, 4, 9, 32 and 43; stoppers at 31, 44, 45, 87 and 119 (exact one-sided Mann-Whitney p 0.016; rho between cells at t=64 and the coalescence generation +0.70). A fast burst that then stops needs a timed window: in s4-s8 the p_div genes include slow rate classes (1/16-1/32). That is a coordinated, switch-like change, which N(0, 0.5) mutation steps reach slowly (the evo critique's latch item).

not_working.item: Late growth costs almost nothing in F, so selection does not stop it (why half keep growing)
not_working.evidence: At T 1024, stopping growth at 768 gives s0 +0.05 ± 0.03, s1 +0.02 ± 0.03, s2 +0.07 ± 0.04, s3 +0.15 ± 0.03 and s9 +0.19 ± 0.04. Averaged over the T draw (768/1024/1536), the best stop time gains s0 0, s1 0, s2 +0.05, s3 +0.42 and s9 +0.53. A selected genome's 7-life score has an SE of about 0.75, so only s3 and s9 are measurably overgrown, at about 0.6-0.7 SE. Oracle caps at 74 vs 122 cells differ by less than 0.5 F in the growers.
not_working.likely_cause: Bounded growth is optimal from physics plus costs, but the optimum is broad. In SPECK a cell living the whole life costs c_live*T/R_cap = 0.02*1024/500 = 0.041 captures (v1: 0.205), so one extra capture per life pays for about 24 cells. Weak circuits gain little from size and lose little from it. Do not raise c_live to sharpen the optimum: the router (122 cells) leads the reflex (56 cells) by only +2.25, so at c_live 0.04 the lead falls to about +0.93, and at 0.06 the router loses (about -0.39).

not_working.item: No evolved body regulates its size; development is open-loop (growth rate x growth window)
not_working.evidence: Kill 25% of cells (E5). Stoppers regrow only a small share of the lost cells. At t=600: s4 33%, s5 35%, s6 0%, s7 6%, s8 11%, at a cost of -2.2 to -2.8 F. Even during the burst, at t=40: s5 39%, s6 25%, s7 20%, s8 21%; s4 ends with fewer births than its control. Growers at t=600 regrow 56-83%, but only because they are still growing. Part of the dF comes from losing the centre or hotspot cell.
not_working.likely_cause: Nothing in the world ever removes cells (0 deaths in every SPECK best), so nothing selects for regulation. The tissue is sealed (morphogen ships only to known contacts), so no local signal reports body size. The evolved stop is a timed window plus contact count, not a size readout. This is why the pre-pilot critique's open-edge morphogen leak has no job yet (see D-wound-world).

not_working.item: The hidden towers are pure cost and come from a juvenile by-product
not_working.evidence: hidden_off after development (forked at 256, frozen) changes F by exactly 0.000 in s0, s3, s4, s6, s7 and s8, and by at most +0.03 ± 0.10 elsewhere. Growing the same genomes with no hidden planes (catch_speck_l2) gains +0.21 on average (0.00 to +0.93; positive in 9 of 9 nonzero cases). s6 gains +0.93 ± 0.13, which matches the living cost of its 45 hidden cells (0.89 F/unit). Only act cells born with p_div > 0 ever bud hidden cells; 81-100% of act cells are born that way (they inherit their sense mother's divide-upward state). The first hidden bud comes at a median act-cell age of 1.4-2.5 units in s1, s3, s5, s7, s8 and s9 (59-100% within 4 units) (e7).
not_working.likely_cause: (1) The juvenile phenotype: a daughter starts from her mother's genes and decides on division at her first tick, after one gene update with lam <= 1/2. (2) First-tick blindness: see the next item. (3) SPECK gives depth no job. A hidden cell touches only the one cell below it, which adds two hops of d0 for nothing. Interior act cells already serve as free interneurons, because the body needs them as filler and their twitches pull nothing.

not_working.item: Birth artefacts: claims made before the mother can know any contact, and gene splits on rejected claims
not_working.evidence: A newborn learns its contacts only at t_birth + 2 d_min = +1.0 (LIFE_ABI 15), but its first tick falls at t_birth + U*P_n with P_n about 2. About half of first ticks therefore read n_view = 0 and see every slot as open. In the fast-burst bodies, 6-15% of all births come from such blind claims (s5 14.4%, s7 14.6%, s6 6.3%, s8 5.8%), including 24-34% of act cells in s5 and s7 and 23-35% of hidden cells in s5, s7 and s8. Slow growers are at <= 2.4% (e8). Rejected claims are 3-16 per life, 7-9% of claims, in s5, s6 and s7 (e7). Each one moves the mother's genes by -asym*Q with no daughter produced (kernel.c 938-943; REJECT only clears claim_pending).
not_working.likely_cause: The first-tick phase rule lets a newborn act before causality allows it to know its surroundings. The contact count, the brake every lineage evolved, reads 'isolated' exactly when a cell is newest. The partition is applied when the claim is sent, not when it succeeds (the pre-pilot devbio item 6(d); now shown to matter in the best bodies).

not_working.item: Genome-driven death exists but is never used
not_working.evidence: The p_die knockout gives 0.00 in every body, and no SPECK best has any deaths. The only measured case where death would pay is removing inert hidden cells: at most +0.93 F in s6, +0.34 in s5, <= 0.22 elsewhere. That is an upper bound from the L2 regrowth, and it is near or below selection's resolution (SE about 0.75).
not_working.likely_cause: The world gives death nothing to do: no turnover, no wounds, no task that rewards removing cells. The founder p_die offset sits about 2 below threshold. Pilot data support the pre-pilot verdict on this item: leave the prior alone until a task rewards removal.

not_working.item: Synapse direction is bought through a morphogen gradient, which is costly and entangled with division placement
not_working.evidence: All four dissected bodies make up-excites/down-inhibits synapses from a standing vertical gradient through 1 + a_c*s_hat. The a_gain knockout costs -3.3 to -10.0 F in 5 of 10 SPECK bests (s5 -10.0, s6 -9.8, s7 -8.5, s3 -3.7, s2 -3.3). Secretion costs s5 0.29 F/unit, about the living cost of 14.5 cells. Swapping the planes' secretion in v1 s5 flips the vertical signs (-3.76). The same s_hat field also steers division placement.
not_working.likely_cause: No knob lets a cell weigh vertical input apart from lateral input (zeta does this only for placement). Pilot data support the pre-pilot devbio and neuro polarity items. The inherited-division-axis variant has no evidence for or against.

not_working.item: The act plane is a copy of the sense plane minus the columns that never budded (mild)
not_working.evidence: Motor-less sense fringes of 6-32 cells (s8: 32, 31% of the body). Act-plane holes average 1.5-1.75 per life in s1 and s9, with 7-10 act cells around them pulling inward toward the hole (e2). The only SPECK best whose act cells divide in-plane, s6, has 0 holes.
not_working.likely_cause: Act cells switch division off after their juvenile window, so the motor plane cannot fill its own gaps. This is a lineage constraint, and only s4 turned the fringe into a gain.

proposals.title: Add no size-stop rule; judge bounded growth by a stop-time panel; keep the cell price
proposals.change: (1) Replace the growing-share readout (GB11) in the pilot analysis with a stop-time panel: paired division_off forks at T/2 and 3T/4, F over the whole life, averaged over the T_choices draw, 768 lives (code: review/dev/e1_stop_growth.py). A seed's growth counts as near-optimal when the best stop gains <= 0.25 F. (2) Keep c_live 0.02 and R_cap 500 in SPECK. (3) Do not add the open-edge morphogen leak, or any other size rule, as a stop mechanism; it moves to D-wound-world.
proposals.targets: The requirement that bounded growth be optimal from physics plus costs, and the misreading 'half the bodies keep growing'
proposals.evidence: E1: the panel separates 2 measurably overgrown seeds (s3 +0.42, s9 +0.53, selection-weighted) from 3 that grow at no measurable cost (s0, s1, s2 <= +0.05) and 5 that stop. 'Growing 1.00' had lumped all 5 non-stoppers together. A cell costs 0.041 captures per life, so the optimum is broad. Raising c_live to 0.04 would cut the router's +2.25 lead to about +0.93, and 0.06 would reverse it (about -0.39). The pre-pilot energy-store item is weakened: late growth is near-neutral (stopping at 768 gives +0.02 to +0.19 F), so moving the same prices into a cell energy store adds no pressure to stop. The pre-pilot leak item is weakened as a stop fix, since 5 of 10 lineages stop without it.
proposals.expressivity: Nothing is lost; no rule is added. The readout now separates slow development from failure to stop.
proposals.constraints: Analysis only. No locality, clock or designed-behaviour impact, and no approval needed.
proposals.cost: About 30 lines in scripts/catch_pilot_analysis.py. About 10k lives per seed (about 5 min at 4 threads per body on this laptop).
proposals.test: Pre-register for the next pilot: count seeds whose selection-weighted best stop gains > 0.25 F (pilot SPECK L4: 2 of 10). Success means <= 2 of 10 without any size rule.

proposals.title: Keep developmental modes alive past the founder lottery, and score runs by development speed
proposals.change: Use the existing evolutionary machinery and add no rule. Split the 32 parents into 2-4 demes that exchange 1 migrant every 10 generations for the first 150 generations, or reuse the ladder's fresh-founder immigrants (evolve.immigrants). Report per seed a developmental outcome: cells at t=64, share of final size at t=256, and whether growth stopped (growing share <= 0.05).
proposals.targets: Slow development in half the lineages (the largest developmental F loss), and bounded growth
proposals.evidence: F rank-correlates with early size (rho 0.94-0.96) but not with final size (0.13). Growers coalesced to one breed at generation 2-43 (median 9), stoppers at 31-119 (median 45), exact p 0.016. Timing alone costs growers about 0.5 F, and their mature F is also lower (e10). The evo critique's population-structure item makes the same call; this adds a developmental outcome to measure.
proposals.expressivity: Nothing is lost. More developmental programmes (fast burst, timed window) stay reachable.
proposals.constraints: Selection-level only; nothing changes inside a life. Within the standing approval for minor tweaks.
proposals.cost: Demes need about 40-80 lines in src/evolve.py if the ladder's immigrant path cannot be reused. Same compute per run.
proposals.test: 10-seed SPECK L4 A/B against the pilot matrix (same seeds and generations). Pre-register: seeds with fast burst then stop (cells at t=64 >= 20 and growing share <= 0.05), pilot 5 of 10, target >= 8 of 10; and median final F >= +4.91.

proposals.title: A newborn listens before it acts: first tick after 2 d_min, gene split at ACK, and an instant gene class
proposals.change: (a) A newborn's first tick moves from t_birth + U*P_n to t_birth + 2 d_min + U*P_n; the zygote and initial cells are unchanged. (b) The mother's -asym*Q is applied when the ACK arrives, using asym stored at the claim; a REJECT leaves her genes unchanged, and c_div is still charged. (c) Extend decode_lambda by one fast class, lam = 1 (g = sigma(b + Wx) at the tick), for raw x < -3.5. A newborn can then read its plane cue and contacts within one tick. This mirrors the pre-pilot critique's frozen class at the slow end.
proposals.targets: Hidden towers, blind claims and rejects, lineage marks blurred by rejected claims, and clean causal rules
proposals.evidence: In the fast-burst bodies, 6-15% of births come from claims made before the mother could know any contact, including 24-34% of act cells in s5 and s7 and 23-35% of hidden cells in s5, s7 and s8 (e8). Rejects are 7-9% of claims in s5, s6 and s7, and each shifts the mother's genes with no daughter. Only act cells born with p_div > 0 bud hidden cells, at a median age of 1.4-2.5 units (e7). Hidden cells cost +0.21 F on average, up to +0.93 (e4). Supports the pre-pilot devbio item 6(d), now quantified on the best bodies.
proposals.expressivity: Gains genes that read identity in one tick (combinational logic). Loses only acting blind in the first ~1 unit after birth, which evolved bodies use for at most 15% of births and which buys about 1 unit per cell generation.
proposals.constraints: (a) and (b) follow the causality floor: no cell acts on knowledge it cannot have yet. All three are local, keep each cell's own clock and random phase (no shared clock), and design no role. Old genomes with raw lam < -3.5 change class (rare). This is an ABI bump and re-prices growing bodies, including the hand GS5 grower, so the GB/GS gates must be rerun. It sits within the standing minor-tweak approval, but tell the user.
proposals.cost: About 20 kernel lines plus the same in the reference; ABI note; test vectors (a rejected claim leaves g bitwise unchanged; an instant gene equals sigma). Gate rerun about 30-60 min at 8 threads.
proposals.test: First re-score the 10 SPECK bests on 1024 lives and report dF. Then a 10-seed SPECK L4 A/B. Pre-register: (i) median hidden cells per final best <= 50% of the control's; (ii) rejects per life <= 1 in every final best; (iii) reached-skill count not more than 2 seeds below the control; (iv) kernel equals reference bitwise on the growth gates.

proposals.title: One signed apical-basal gain knob, the vertical twin of zeta, so chemistry stops doing synapse polarity
proposals.change: Add one knob u (q8 grid in [-2, 2]; founder value exactly 0, readout std 0 as for the other fixed knobs): w_eff[d] = q8(w_c * (1 + a_c*s_hat_d - u*dz_d)), with dz = +1 for the up slot, -1 for the down slot and 0 in-plane. u = +1.5 gives x2.5 from below and x(-0.5) from above, the pattern every dissected body evolved. Pad old genomes with u = 0, which is bitwise neutral.
proposals.targets: Direction-specific synapses at low cost; chemistry freed for position and size information; less coupling between synapse sign and division placement
proposals.evidence: All four dissected bodies build vertical synapse signs from a morphogen gradient. The a_gain knockout costs 3.3-10.0 F in 5 of 10 SPECK bests. s5 spends 0.29 F/unit on secretion, about 14.5 cells. Swapping secretion between planes flips the signs (v1 s5, -3.76). One s_hat field drives both gain and placement. Supports the pre-pilot devbio 2, neuro 1 and evo apical-basal items; the inherited-axis variant has no evidence yet.
proposals.expressivity: Gains vertical-specific gain without chemistry. Nothing is lost: u = 0 recovers today's law, and a_c*s_hat stays for in-plane direction.
proposals.constraints: Local: a cell knows which of its own slots are vertical, as zeta already uses. No clock, no role. Adds 17 genome entries. ABI bump; neutral for padded genomes. Overlaps the neuro lens, so ship one version.
proposals.cost: A few lines in derive (kernel and reference), a decode row, a pad, a test that u = 0 is bitwise neutral, and gate reruns.
proposals.test: 10-seed SPECK L4 A/B. Pre-register: median a_gain knockout loss in final bests <= 1 F (pilot: 5 of 10 at >= 3.3); median secretion cost per final best lower than the control's; median F >= the control's.

proposals.title: In-life cell loss, so regulation, maintenance and genome-driven death have a job (with an open-edge morphogen leak arm)
proposals.change: Implement the reserved world key kill_rate as a per-cell hazard: each cell draws an exponential death time at birth from its own key. Death cause is external; the neighbours' DIED notices and refill by claims work as for apoptosis. Calibrate it to about 20-25% loss per 1024 life (h about 2.5e-4 per unit). Run three SPECK arms: control, hazard, and hazard plus the critique's open-edge leak (m*q lost through each open in-plane face, k_m floor 5e-4).
proposals.targets: Size regulation and regeneration, robust development, genome-driven death actually used, and a first step toward the generalisation the user wants
proposals.evidence: No evolved body regulates its size. After losing 25% of their cells, stoppers regrow 0-35% (t=600) or 20-39% (t=40) of them and lose 2.2-4.7 F (e5, e5b). Apoptosis is unused (0 deaths; p_die knockout 0). The leak has no job in a world where nothing perturbs size, because growers' stop-time landscape is flat. That weakens the pre-pilot leak item as a stop fix but keeps it as the physical size readout for regulation. Supports the evo verdict on the apoptosis item: wait for a task that rewards removing or replacing cells.
proposals.expressivity: Gains selection for size-restoring growth, refill and turnover. The leak arm replaces the sealed-tissue rule with open faces (rule count unchanged) and adds a size cue genes can read. Nothing is lost at hazard 0.
proposals.constraints: A world hazard, not adversarial and not a designed role. Each death uses the cell's own key and refill uses the existing local claims, so it is local, asynchronous and clockless. It is a new world feature, so it NEEDS USER APPROVAL. The leak is a chemistry-rule swap and needs a section-15 justification.
proposals.cost: About 50-80 kernel lines plus the reference for kill_rate; about 30 for the leak; gate reruns. Three arms of 10 seeds take about 3x the SPECK L4 arm (about 90 run-hours on this laptop, or 2-3 h on one 192-core box at $10-30).
proposals.test: Pre-register on final bests: (i) regrow >= 70% of a 25% wound at t=600 within 300 units in >= 5 of 10 seeds (pilot stoppers: 0 of 5); (ii) growing share <= 0.05 in >= 5 of 10; (iii) F in the hazard-free world within 0.5 of the pilot median; (iv) genome-driven deaths > 0 per life in >= 3 of 10. The leak arm beats hazard-only on (i).

proposals.title: Make hidden planes worth building through geometry and a memory need, not by forcing roles
proposals.change: Keep L_max 4 (the user's design) and add no rule to suppress or force towers. (a) When the radius gene arrives, measure radius in 3D, so that at radius 2 a hidden cell also contacts the 6 sites diagonally below it: it hears 7 act cells instead of 1, which makes it a natural pooling layer. (b) Add a task variant that needs persistent activity without sensing or twitching, for example SPECK-blink: the target's receptor emission stops for gaps of about Exp(10) every Exp(30) while the target keeps moving and can still be captured.
proposals.targets: Use of hidden cells, routing and computation beyond a one-hop reflex
proposals.evidence: hidden_off after development is 0.000 in 6 of 10 and |dF| <= 0.03 in the rest. The no-hidden-plane regrowth gains +0.21 on average (up to +0.93) (e4). Hidden cells are juvenile by-products (e7, e8). A hidden cell has one vertical contact, so any computation through it pays 2 extra hops of d0. Interior act cells already provide free interneurons, because they are filler and their twitches pull nothing (s5). In SPECK, in-plane computation never needs an extra layer. The pre-pilot simplify item called hidden planes overcomplicated: pilot data support it as a cost (about 0.2 F tax), but the remedy is giving them a job, not removing them.
proposals.expressivity: Gains convergent fan-in for hidden cells and a reason for memory. Nothing is lost.
proposals.constraints: The 3D metric is a lattice-geometry choice inside the planned radius gene, and stays local (contacts within radius 2). The blink task is a new world variant and NEEDS USER APPROVAL. No designed roles.
proposals.cost: (a) is part of the radius-gene work (contact tables). (b) is about 20 kernel lines (an emission gate on the receptor stream) plus gates.
proposals.test: Pre-register for the blink arm (or radius-2 arm): hidden_off after development costs >= 0.5 F (z >= 3) in >= 3 of 10 final bests, and the L4 body beats its own L2 regrowth in >= 3 of 10 (pilot: 0 of 10).

proposals.title: One life, several world episodes: develop once, be judged across varied conditions
proposals.change: A life of about 4 x 768 units. At unannounced switch times, the world redraws its parameters from a set (sigma in {0.4, 0.6, 1.0}, v_t in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}, optionally the existing second blob as a decoy, b2_value < 0). Cells see only their receptors, as now. Selection scores the whole life.
proposals.targets: Generalisation and adapting to new situations; growth that stays bounded over long lives; compute that scales with task variety
proposals.evidence: Second-half F exceeds first-half F by 0.8-3.1 in every SPECK best (e10), so in a 1024 life development and warm-up weigh heavily. Longer lives sharpen the stop optimum: stopping at 512 averaged over T gains s3 +0.42 and s9 +0.53, against +0.12 and +0.24 at T 1024 alone (e1). Growers reach 250-320 cells at T 1536, and they also drive the compute bill (CPU is linear in cell-time).
proposals.expressivity: Gains pressure for in-life adaptation (s2 already adapts its gain to crowding) and for regulation. Nothing is lost.
proposals.constraints: Still one continuous life with local sensing and no clock in cells; the switch times are world events. A task-design change, so it NEEDS USER APPROVAL.
proposals.cost: The world draws already exist; per-episode redraws are about 30-50 kernel lines plus the reference. Each life costs about 3x a 1024 life in CPU, but replaces separate lives at equal compute, and bounded bodies keep cell-time down.
proposals.test: Equal-compute A/B on SPECK. Pre-register: held-out score on unseen parameter combinations higher than the single-world arm by > 3 paired SE; growing share <= 0.05 in >= 5 of 10 seeds.

reviews.notes: Keep (1): random tie-breaking with its own generator. It REMOVES an implicit hard-coded rule (on exact ties, parents win through a stable sort) and is neutral without ties. Keep (2): one size-adaptive L per generation keeps CRN; it is harness-only. Modify (3): rank re-screened founders by F alone. Drop 'prefer multi-cell earners' and phenotype labels (end size, clicks): they are a selection criterion outside fitness that rewards multicellularity, which is design. If diversity is wanted, use genotype distance or keep the top k by F from each founder batch. Modify (4): the founder n_max 256 trips the guard, which ends the life and charges c_live*n_max. That is a hard size bound on founders and penalises founders that grow past 256. Accept it only as a compute guard, after checking on at least 4 founder batches that no top-k founder would exceed 256 cells. No approval needed.

Harness only, outside any life, with no rule effect. Bitwise resume is the right gate. Constraint: rank runs for halving and extension by valid F only, never by mechanism readouts (lateral share, hidden use, size), or run-level selection becomes a designed-mechanism filter. Keep pre-registered counts on the full fixed seed set, as proposed. Absorbs the run-level half of D-dev-diversity.

No organism change, and declining parent records and single-stage selection is the conservative choice. Fast mode is acceptable only if gates and golden hashes keep the full build, as stated. The optional 2+5 A/B costs $50-80 for at most about 19% fewer lives: run it only if compute binds.

Split it. (a) duplicates T-fast-conduction: fold it in. (b) duplicates T-hidden-L2: L_max 4 is the user's design and needs approval. (c) the income lead over reflex@hollow3 and the lateral_off share of that lead are fine ONLY as reported readouts. Never enter them in selection or in run-portfolio ranking, since that would reward a mechanism. Keep (c) and merge the rest.

Turning on dup/del with bitwise-neutral copies is config of an already-designed, already-tested mechanism. It adds evolvable capacity without adding an organism rule, which the minimal-hard-coding goal favours. Run it alone first. Test the silent-gene-targeted large steps (a new search-operator rule) as a second arm only if plain duplication shows no new genes wired by generation 300. Drop the edit to the hand seed's secretion: seeded arms inject designed behaviour and should stay controls, not something we keep re-engineering. Tell the user, since the effective gene count changes.

Canonical id for d0 0.5 / d_min 0.25; R-fast-conduction and E-routing-value(a) duplicate it. It is a world constant: no rule, clock or channel. Measurement only, which is good. The A2 filter, though, admits only worlds where the hand router beats the reflex, so the task gets chosen to favour a mechanism we designed. critiques.critic:
Experimentalist lens. I re-checked the lens numbers against RESULTS.md, analysis.md and the lens output files, and ran four small new checks. All new work is under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-jgon-project-ml-cell-dev/aefb0c66-3af5-49c4-936c-154d6434706c/scratchpad/review/xp/ (cputime.py; proj.py with proj_s4/s5/s8.jsonl). Life seeds come from fresh_seeds at base 36,600,000.

WHAT HOLDS UP
- The tie rule (src/evolve.py:516/523).
- Hidden planes are inert and cost about 0.2-0.3 F. Dev e4 gives +0.21 mean over 10 bodies and evo E4 gives +0.32 over 7. Only s6 is large (+0.93).
- Faster conduction helps every body at no CPU cost. My clean timing gives 0.9-1.0x CPU per life.
- delta and tau_tr do nothing.
- The D stop-time panel.
- runlevel.py reproduces exactly: Spearman 0.21/0.58/0.79/0.94 at generations 50/100/200/300, median late slope +0.45 per 100 generations.
- The P0-4 compute claim. I timed it directly (threads 1, load about 1.8). Same-size bodies run 1.7-1.9x faster (s4 0.053 -> 0.028-0.031 CPU-s per life; s7 0.054 -> 0.029). The lens's "ticks are 68-74% of CPU" split is wrong, though. A two-term fit across P0 arms, which breaks the collinearity between ticks and events, gives 0.54 us per tick and 177 ns per heap event. That puts ticks at about 45% and receptor candidates at about 35% of CPU. P0 4 wins anyway because it also removes packet events.
- Absolute CPU per life on the idle laptop is about 0.05 s for 95-100-cell bodies. The audit's 0.1 was measured under load, so the rental estimates are about 2x conservative.

MISREAD OR OVERSTATED
(1) "The gap to the reflex is cell upkeep, not skill" (evo lens). The oracle-capped size curve for s5 (results.csv) gives 5.47 ± 0.58 at a 74-cell cap against 8.43 ± 0.90 at 122. s5's algorithm needs its cells, so this is a per-cell efficiency gap in the computation, not a small economy trait that drifts. Only s6's 47 hidden cells are true dead weight.
(2) "Per-face averages keep F, so a face-gain table expresses 90-100% of what chemistry built" (rules lens). That test kept 6 numbers per cell (per channel x per face). The proposed primitives keep fewer. My projection arms (reference simulator, freeze at fork, 32 paired lives each):
- s5, full per-face table: +0.04 ± 0.51.
- s5, rank-1 w_c*k_face (R-face-gains as specified): -11.6 ± 0.6 (captures 16.5 -> 0.4).
- s5, one shared u (D-axial-gain): -11.8 ± 0.6.
- s5, per-channel u with lateral pinned to the mean of up and down: -4.2 ± 0.9, even though the relative residual is only 0.4%.
- s4 and s8: every form matches the full table within noise.
- Per-face averaging alone is not free either: s8 -1.38 ± 0.36, s4 -1.13 ± 0.65.
So any face primitive must be per channel.
(3) "Evolved bodies are 2-3x more fragile specialists" (task lens). The ratio is taken on F, which carries the bigger bodies' fixed costs. Using the lens's own E1 table, capture retention over the sparse/noisy/fast/decoy worlds is reflex 0.58, router 0.52, s5 0.51, s2 0.53, s4 0.48, s7 0.47. Real fragility shows up mainly in the noisy world (s4).
(4) The "genetic correlation 0.25" between base and twin is a raw correlation of 16-life means. Corrected for noise it is 0.54 (bootstrap 90% CI 0.33-0.85). In twin the genetic correlation of F with end size flips to -0.61, against +0.37 in base. So the extra selectable variance a twin-heavy family exposes is mostly "be smaller", which points toward the reflex and away from size-hungry pooling.
(5) The P_fix and purge figures (E2) come from an unvalidated simulator. Its sibling load model overpredicted about 100x, and the audit's models overpredict 10-30x. "Ranking noise is not the bottleneck" is therefore a hypothesis. The DFE behind "near mutation-selection balance" uses one parent (s5) with 40 mutants and SE 0.34 per mutant. The non-broken mean is -0.14 ± about 0.08.
(6) T-click-decision's "s5 beats the reflex at c_miss 100" uses a reflex tuned at c_miss 10. The router's lead does not move with c_miss (+2.15), so a higher miss price does not reward routing.
(7) The d0 0.5 routing leads (+3.3 to +3.5) were measured with neither the router nor the reflex re-tuned. LIFE_GATES says so explicitly.

DESIGN PROBLEMS SHARED BY MANY PROPOSALS
- Power. The between-run SD of final F is 1.52. A 10-vs-10 seed A/B has an SE of about 0.68 on the mean difference and more on medians. Detecting 0.5 F at 80% power takes about 145 seeds per arm; detecting 1 F takes about 36. Most of the pre-registered "median F within or above 0.3-0.5 F" criteria are coin flips. Count criteria like 8/10 vs 5/10 are not significant either (Fisher p about 0.35).
- Tests that pass by construction:
  - fast-conduction F vs the pilot: physics alone adds about +0.9;
  - L2 F >= L4: L2 removes a known 0.2-0.3 F cost;
  - "active genes > 8" with dup rate above del rate: mutation bias alone fills the slots.
- Historical controls. Several tests compare new arms with the pilot, which ran on older code under a laptop load, instead of a concurrent control.
- Bundling. Putting face gains, pruning, time laws, birth hygiene, fast conduction, L2, ties and duplication into one ABI 4 would make the next pilot impossible to attribute.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE
Stage 0: exact harness work, no approval needed.
- Random tie-breaking.
- Fast kernel mode for evolution.
- Checkpoint and resume.
- Bitwise-exact early receptor rejection.
- Readouts: income lead over the reflex, the shortlist's split-half reliability, the stop panel and developmental speed.
Stage 1: cheap decisive diagnostics.
- Re-tune the reflex and the router at d0 0.5 / d_min 0.25.
- Extend s5, s6, s7 and s8 to 1,000 generations.
- A router-seeded SPECK arm.
- A continuation with 4x lives against standard lives from the same pilot populations.
- A niche map that includes s5 and its lateral_off twin.
Stage 2: one change per arm against a concurrent control.
- Use mechanism-level primary endpoints with large effects: knockout use of a new primitive, the lateral_off share, the count of routers.
- Use 20-30+ seeds per arm on rented cores.

reviews.notes:
The four changes are not equally backed.
(1) Random tie-breaking. The bug is confirmed in code and in the data: 244-364 total frozen generations in v1 L4 s1, s2, s4 and s7 (longest stretches 36-256). It is a few lines and exact when there are no ties. Ship it now with a unit test; it needs no A/B.
(2)-(4) Size-adaptive L, founder re-screen and founder cap. These target v1. SPECK already solves the start (10/10 grow), so v1 is off the critical path.
The causal story is mixed. L2 s2 and L4 s2 had identical founders and still reached different fates, so the founder lottery is not the main driver.
The pre-registered test is not decisive. 6/10 against the pilot's 4/10 gives Fisher p about 0.65, and the pilot is a historical control.
If v1 matters, use 30 seeds per arm, which is cheap at about 1 s per 2-cell generation. Better still, resume the four frozen pilot populations from population.json under random ties against a frozen-tie control with matched RNG, and measure generations to more than 4 cells.
Do not bundle the four changes. A pass would not say which one worked.

Checkpoint and resume is the highest-value harness item. The audit flags that spot capacity loses whole runs, and population.json already exists for every pilot run.
Extending s5, s6, s7 and s8 to 1,000 generations (about $4-6 rented) is the cheapest decisive test of whether the routing gap is 'time' or 'a barrier'. The late slopes (s5 +0.66, s6 +0.56, s7 +0.35, s8 +0.41 per 100 generations) reproduce. The pre-registered criterion (beat the reflex by more than 3 SE on 1,024 lives, with lateral_off removing at least half of the lead) is binary and meaningful.
Modifications:
(a) A pilot-derived population lacks the saved torch RNG state, so it cannot continue bitwise. Label the extension 'continued', not 'resumed'.
(b) The halving rule would have cut a strong run. At generation 200, s6 ranked 6/10 on valid F (3.3) and finished at 6.22, third best on 1,024 lives. Use a lenient first cut (keep the top 3/4) or a rule that also weighs slope.
(c) Also report income lead and cells, so a body that wins only by trimming cells is not counted as computation.

The parts to adopt now are exact and verified: fast kernel mode (1.24-1.35x, ledger-identical in 62/62 lives) and job-layout freedom.
The founder cap and clone forks every 50 generations are cheap, but they are not exact; they need a stated rationale, not an A/B.
The argument for keeping 3 + 4 rests on E2 and purge.py. Those are unvalidated simulations, and the sibling load model was off about 100x. Treat 'do not change ranking' as a default, not a finding.
If ranking matters, run the decisive version: continue from the same pilot population under 3 + 4 versus 4x lives versus 2 + 5, 3 replicates each, about 50 generations, and score progress in true F on 512 fresh lives.
The proposed 10-seed A/B with a 0.3 F margin cannot resolve the question (between-run SD 1.52).

(a) Faster conduction duplicates T-fast-conduction and R-fast-conduction. (b) L_max 2 duplicates T-hidden-L2 and R-hidden-l2.
(c) The income readout is the valuable new piece. Keep it. s5 earns 9.65 against the reflex's 9.95 (econ.json), so income lead plus the lateral_off share of that lead separates skill from body economy. It is about 30 lines.
Correction to the premise. 'Bodies pay for router-sized bodies but earn reflex income' is right. 'The gap is economy noise that selection barely sees' is wrong for s5: its oracle-capped curve falls from 8.43 ± 0.90 at 122 cells to 5.47 ± 0.58 at 74. The cells feed its pooling algorithm, so trimming them is not a 0.1 F drift step. The barrier is per-cell efficiency of the evolved algorithm.
The test 'median F not lower' passes by physics at d0 0.5. Score F relative to references re-tuned in the same world.

The diagnosis is solid: exactly 8 active genes in every unseeded best, 5 in every seeded best, and seeded secretion stuck at -800.
The benefit is unproven. The critique verdict already noted that the 13-gene router is a hand-written boolean design and that gene count has not been shown to bind.
The DFE argument for aiming row-scale only at silent genes is reasonable, but it rests on one parent (s5) and 40 mutants.
The main pre-registered criterion, 'active genes > 8 in 4/6 seeds', passes by mutation bias alone (dup 0.02 > del 0.01). Replace it with:
(i) the number of duplicate-derived genes whose knockout costs more than 0.5 F at z > 3 in final bests;
(ii) the share of those with self-weight of 4 or more and a role (crisp switches);
(iii) speed of development and evolution (generation to F >= 4) against a concurrent control, as a secondary measure.
Drop 'median F within 0.3' as a criterion; 6 seeds per arm cannot resolve it.
Also run the cheap seeded-chemistry fix (secretion near -5 instead of -800) as its own small arm, not bundled with this one.

T-family dominates this proposal. T-family reuses existing world keys (b2 twin and decoy), whereas a multi-target kernel needs new code and gates.
The information-per-CPU claim was an estimate ('1.5-2x at 3 targets, not measured'), and the task lens's measured TWIN data refute it. A second target raises captures only 1.38x (19.1 -> 26.4) and cuts per-life SD at equal income by about 15%. It also shrinks the router's lead from +2.17 to +0.37, so density favours the reflex.
The goal of task variety for generalisation survives; carry it in T-family, after T-niche-map.

The effect is real and free. Pilot forks: router +1.99, reflex +0.99, every body +0.14 to +1.70. My timing: CPU per life 0.9-1.0x.
The test is flawed.
(1) 'Median final F >= pilot +4.91 + 0.5' passes on physics alone, since existing bodies already gain a median of about +0.9 without re-evolving. It also compares with a historical control.
(2) Both references were untuned at d0 0.5; LIFE_GATES says explicitly that neither side was re-tuned. The +3.3 to +3.5 lead is therefore provisional.
Modify: first re-tune both the reflex and the router at d0 0.5 / d_min 0.25 (about 3-4 CPU-h; retune.py exists), and go ahead only if the re-tuned lead is at least +3.0 with lateral_off removing at least 50%. That is R-fast-conduction's test, the best of the three duplicates.
Then pre-register only in-world-relative endpoints: the count of seeds beating the re-tuned reflex by more than 3 SE, and the lateral_off share, with a concurrent d0 1 control.
Interactions: d_min 0.25 halves the newborn blind window (see D-birth-hygiene), and it changes growth timing, so rerun the GB gates.

It is cheap (10-30 CPU-min per map), it is measurement only, and it prevents launching another DECOY-style cliff. The E1 data show the router's lead depends on the world: +2.17 base; about 0 in twin, near and decoy-lite; -1.28 sparse; +3.51 fast conduction.
Modifications:
(a) Add the evolved pooling body (s5) and its lateral_off fork to the reference set. The hand router is the wrong proxy for the computation evolution actually finds, and 'lateral_off removes X% here' is a direct readout of where local computation pays.
(b) Hand references are tuned only for base. Re-tune them at the corners of any range chosen for a family, at least once, before using the map to pass or fail A2.
(c) Report capture or income retention alongside F. F ratios mostly reflect cost structure (see the critic summary).

The goal (generalisation) is the user's, and the machinery reuses the existing per-life keys, which keeps CRN. Some evidence is misread, though.
(1) The 'genetic correlation 0.25' between base and twin is a raw correlation of 16-life means. Corrected for noise it is 0.54 (bootstrap 90% CI 0.33-0.85).
(2) The extra reliability a twin share brings (0.18 -> 0.51) comes from heritable variance along body size. The genetic correlation of F with end size is -0.61 in twin against +0.37 in base. A family heavy in twin would select smaller, reflex-like bodies, against the pooling computation that needs size (s5 loses about 3 F capped at 74 cells).
(3) The 'evolved bodies keep only 0.16-0.24' motivation is overstated. In captures, retention is 0.47-0.53 against the reflex's 0.58.
Modify:
- Run it only after T-niche-map.
- Draw ranges where s5's lateral_off share stays at least at its base value.
- Keep the twin and decoy share small.
- Pre-register in-world-relative held-out endpoints as differences, not ratios (a ratio to the reflex blows up near 0).
- Use 20+ seeds per arm or a continuation design, because the 10-seed A/B is underpowered.
Priority: next, not now.

The proposal is correct and nearly free.
The proxy evidence is weak inside the near-neutral cloud. Cross-half r is 0.09 for the proxies against 0.17-0.19 for F, with SE about 0.06 at n 244. The evidence is strong across all genomes (0.14 and 0.49 against 0.77). The ICC point is also right: proxies are more heritable along directions nearly orthogonal to F, so they would be selected for parking near targets rather than catching.
The decision rule for re-opening shaping is a good pre-registration.
Add the readouts to the same analysis patch as E-routing-value (c) and D-stop-panel.

An implementation-only change. Step 1 is bitwise exact; step 2 is exact in distribution, with a KS test plus a check on the reference bodies' F.

Analysis only and well evidenced. e1_b reproduces: s3 +0.42 and s9 +0.53 selection-weighted, s4 about 0 at every stop time. It separates measurable overgrowth (2/10) from near-neutral late growth (3/10) and stoppers (5/10), which the 'share growing 1.00' readout lumped together.

A duplicate of R-face-gains with less expressivity, and my projection test settles the choice.

If minimalism is preferred over s5-type solutions, a single u is defensible only knowing it leaves s5-type wiring to chemistry. Otherwise adopt the per-channel up/down gains (modified R-face-gains).

critiques.missing:
1. Power analysis and concurrent controls. The between-run SD of final F is 1.52. Detecting 0.5 F at 80% power needs about 145 seeds per arm; 1 F needs about 36. Re-base every A/B on one of:
- mechanism endpoints with large effects (knockout use of a new primitive, the lateral_off share, chain-depth counts);
- binary or count endpoints (routers found);
- continuation designs that start every arm from the same pilot population.
Always use a concurrent control, never the historical pilot.
2. A router-seeded SPECK arm: seed the GS5 GRN router genome, 3-5 seeds, 150-200 generations. If selection holds or improves the router, the barrier is reachability. If it decays toward pooling or the reflex, the barrier is selection, noise or economy. Nobody proposed this, and it is the cheapest decisive test of the evo-lens versus task-lens disagreement.
3. A direct test of whether noise is the bottleneck: from the same pilot population (for example s5), run about 50 generations at standard lives against 4x lives, 3 replicates each, and score true-F gain on 512 fresh lives. This replaces the unvalidated E2 and purge models (the sibling load model was off about 100x).
4. Re-tune the references in every new world before using any routing criterion. All the d0 0.5 leads (+3.3 to +3.5) and the c_miss re-pricing used references tuned at base; LIFE_GATES confirms neither side was re-tuned.
5. Staged attribution. Do not ship face gains, pruning, time laws, birth hygiene, d0, L2, ties and duplication as one ABI-4 pilot. The order should be:
- exact harness work first (ties, fast mode, checkpointing, readouts, early receptor rejection);
- then world constants, with re-tuned references;
- then one organism change per arm.
6. Correct the efficiency framing. s5's size curve (8.43 at 122 cells against 5.47 at 74) shows the evolved algorithm needs its cells. The target is per-cell efficiency of the computation. Add an 'income per cell at fixed body size' readout (oracle caps at 56/74/122 against the reflex) to track progress toward routing.
7. Per-channel structure of any new synapse primitive. My projection shows that rank-1 or shared gains break the best body (s5 -11.6 to -11.8), while a per-channel face table does not (+0.04 ± 0.51).
8. Use the right metrics:
- capture or income retention, not F ratios, for 'generalisation' (capture retention is 0.47-0.53 for evolved bodies against 0.58 for the reflex);
- noise-corrected cross-world genetic correlations (0.54, not 0.25).
9. A scaling rationale for the user's 'reframe to scale' question:
- My timing says the audit's per-life CPU is about 2x pessimistic (about 0.05 CPU-s per life for about 100-cell bodies on an idle core).
- P0 4 (about 1.8x) and early receptor rejection (receptor candidates are about 35% of CPU by my fit) are the two big exact or near-exact levers, before any task reframing.
- Information per CPU-second should be measured, not estimated. A twin world raised captures only 1.38x.
10. A check that any task family keeps the pooling niche: across the drawn worlds, s5's lateral_off share should not fall below its base value. Otherwise variety may select generalist reflexes, especially since twin-type worlds select for smaller bodies (genetic r(F, size) -0.61).

reviews.notes:
Split it into four parts.
(1) Random tie-break: ship now. It is a few lines, keeps runs bitwise when no ties occur, and is confirmed by the 244-364 frozen generations. It becomes more important under T-family, because per-life percentile ranks create many more exact ties.
(4) Founder n_max 256: ship now. Founder CPU falls about 4x (guard trips were 82% of founder CPU, about 4-5% of pilot compute) and the chosen top 8 are unchanged.
(3) Re-screen: keep it, but rank on F only. Drop 'prefer multi-cell earners / distinct phenotypes'. That is a hand-coded bias toward multicellularity, against 'start small' and minimal hard-coding; diversity belongs in E-portfolio at run level.
(2) Size-adaptive L: defer. It ties lives per generation to body size, which adds a schedule and lets selection strength drift during a run. Its payoff is mainly in v1-like worlds with a small foothold. SPECK already takes off (5/10 grow straight from their founders). Build it only if a small-foothold world stays in the plan.
Compute: net cheaper. Rules: harness only.

Best scale lever on the harness side.

- Successive halving saves an estimated 25-40% against running all 16 runs to the end.

Modifications:
(a) Bundle determinism pinning with resume: ATEN_CPU_CAPABILITY=avx2, pinned torch, the libm fingerprint check (xmachine_check) and the build flags. The audit's verdict calls this a must, because torch.randn and glibc's FMA paths differ by CPU. A run resumed on another machine type is otherwise not bitwise.
(b) Add the audit's elastic thread budget. It removes the single-run tail, about 3.3x fewer rented hours on a 192-thread box per the loop report, though its reviewer attributes most of that to a free job-layout change.
(c) Extending s5, s6, s7 and s8 from population.json is a new run: the generator state was not saved. Label it as a continuation, not a bitwise extension.
(d) Keep the pre-registered counts on the full seed set, as proposed.

Switches on machinery that already exists and is tested. A silent copy is bitwise neutral, so this needs no ABI change and no new organism rule. Compute: the kernel skips rows with lam == 0 (kernel.c:822), and regulation is 9-10% of CPU at 8 genes. Going to about 12 active genes therefore costs at most about +5% per life. The readout already spans all 16 genes.
Modifications:

Changes two constants, adds no rule, and loses no expressivity: delta still adds delay.
The CPU cost is about zero: p0scan modelled 0.97-1.13x, and events per life are unchanged. Three lenses and the pre-pilot critique support it. The router's lead over the reflex grows from +2.17 to +3.51 (+62%), and every evolved body gains.

This entry carries the merged R-fast-conduction and E-routing-value(a).

Very cheap screening. Hand bodies cost 0.01-0.03 CPU-s per life, and a full 11-world x 8-body x 256-life grid took about 15 min, against about 24 CPU-h per 10-seed evolution arm. It replaces failed runs (DECOY's cliff, TWIN's reflex bias) with minutes of measurement. Scripts only; nothing changes inside a life.
Modifications:
(a) Add the evolved bests (s4-s8, the pooling bodies) as reference bodies, not only the hand router. The A2 test 'hand router beats reflex' encodes designed computation as the yardstick and would exclude worlds where only evolved pooling pays (for example 4x background).
(b) Add per-world columns for per-life SD of F, captures per life and CPU per life, so the map also ranks worlds by selection information per CPU-second. This answers the user's question about scaling.

Highest value per cost under my lens.
- It reuses the existing per-life envelope draw (evaluate.py _envelope, keyed by run, purpose, generation and life), so CRN holds.

- It adds no organism rule or kernel code: about 40-60 lines.
- Measured: mixing worlds raises split-half reliability from 0.18 to 0.47-0.51, by exposing heritable variance that a single world hides (genetic SD 0.33 in base, 0.89 in twin).
- It is the user's own generalisation goal.
Modifications:
(a) Specify the percentile's reference set across the two stages: rank among the 256 for stage 1, and among the 64-genome shortlist on all 7 lives for the recheck.
(b) Ship the random tie-break first, because percentiles create exact ties.
(c) Make c_miss a family axis, for example {10, 30, 50}, instead of T-click-decision's ramp. Later add kill_rate (D-wound-world) the same way.
(d) Start with 2-3 axes inside the niche map so a loss of computation can be attributed.
Risk: robust reflexes may out-select fragile computation (retention 0.45 against 0.16-0.24). Keep the lateral_off-share guard as proposed. The family-as-task framing needs the user's confirmation.

Clean: F stays task performance and the cost economy that bounds growth stays intact. The measured reasons hold: dense proxies predict F worse than F itself (+0.09 against +0.17-0.19), and they are more heritable along traits nearly orthogonal to F (parking near targets).
The readouts (shortlist split-half reliability, capture index of dispersion) cost about 20 lines and no compute.
Distinguish two things in the write-up. Rejecting proxy shaping is right. Choosing tasks whose own score has many events per life (a different world, not a shaped term) remains a legitimate scale lever and belongs in the niche map.

The goal (click logic built from neighbours' evidence) is fine. The mechanism, a ramp triggered by population thresholds (median F > 4 and median body > 14), adds hand-set schedule parameters, and it re-prices the size economy in the middle of a run.
The evidence is weaker than it reads:
- The +0.28 lead at c_miss 100 is post-hoc re-pricing against a reflex that was not re-tuned at that price; a tuned reflex would tighten its click threshold.
- The router's lead stays about +2.15 at every price, so the ramp adds no routing pressure.
- Evolved bodies already capture on 49-50% of clicks, so precision is already emergent.
Cleaner: drop the ramp and make c_miss a per-life axis of T-family, for example {10, 30, 50}. Lives at 10 keep the 2-cell rung, there are no thresholds, and selection integrates over prices. Keep the P.chains lateral-hop check as a readout.

The direction is right:
- Within-life variety amortises development. Second-half F exceeds first-half F by 0.8-3.1, and development ends by t of about 100-512.
- Retiring b2's six special keys into one table is a genuine cleanup.
But at 150-250 kernel lines plus the reference, per-type thinning bounds and gates, it is the most expensive world change on the list.
Stage it:

That is about 30-50 lines, the same within-life variety, and a test of whether in-life adaptation (genes_blind fork) appears at all.
(2) Only if mixtures of simultaneous blob types are needed, add the type table at a world-ABI bump that deletes b2.
Per-type thinning matters: each extra type raises receptor candidates, which are already 54% of heap events. Value switches stay gated on taste, as proposed.

Strong evidence:
- Isotropic weights cost s5 -10.10.
- Per-face averages keep F in all four bodies. The SEs are 0.19-0.67, so '90-100%' is within noise but consistent.
- Chemistry-built wiring breaks under clock changes.
The kernel change is about 10 lines in derive() (kernel.c:560-575) plus the decode, using off_z, which already exists. Runtime cost is about 0. Each knob starts at exactly 1, so the change is bitwise neutral for padded genomes.
Cleanliness:
- Bundled with R-prune (drop the tau_tr and chi rows, freeze delta), the knob count stays the same. Present it to the user as 'swap three dead knobs for three face gains' in one ABI-4 bump.
- It opens a staged simplification that nobody proposed: if a_c knockouts in the face-arm bests become null, retire the a_c weight route and the max-normalised shat from w_eff at ABI 5. s_d would stay only for division placement. That is a net loss of a special-case rule.
Prefer it to D-axial-gain: one signed u caps vertical:lateral at about 3:1 and cannot silence lateral input, which is the same limit the pre-pilot critique found for the morphogen route.
Scale: it also gives the radius gene a clean extension (k_lat2).

Removes rules at no measured cost.
- Knockouts on 21 bests: delta at most 0.13, tau_tr at most 0.25, chi null in 19 of 21.
- The freeze is a harness mutation mask (about 20 lines, no ABI change). Removal waits for the ABI-4 bump.
- It removes pleiotropic drift: chi rotates division placement.
- It saves a little readout CPU (the readout is 12-13% of CPU).
Modifications:

Duplicate of T-hidden-L2; see that entry. It needs the user's decision. Keep one L4 control wherever memory pressure is introduced. Once face gains exist, a hidden relay is a k_up/k_down setting, which makes restoring L4 later a cleaner experiment.

Analysis only, with no size rule; it keeps 'bounded growth from physics plus costs' honest. (b) Gene split at ACK: keep, in the ABI-4 bundle. It is a pure causality cleanup (no effect without an outcome), about 10 lines, and fixes a documented artefact: 7-9% of claims are rejected in s5-s7.

This gives genome-driven death, regulation and regeneration a job. Modifications:

(2) Drop the leak arm from the first test. It swaps the sealed-tissue chemistry rule, adds a third arm (+50% of compute), and has no job until the hazard alone fails criterion (i).
Cost: about 50-80 kernel lines plus the reference. Put it in the second ABI batch, after face gains and the time laws, not in the first. It needs user approval.

The principle, giving depth a job instead of forcing roles, fits minimal hard-coding.

Keep L4 only in arms where depth can pay; elsewhere use L2 (T-hidden-L2).

Merged with T-types-epochs as the cheaper first step: redraw scalar world parameters at unannounced Poisson world times, about 30-50 kernel lines. It amortises development across situations: second-half F exceeds first-half F by 0.8-3.1, and the stop optimum sharpens in longer lives. That is a real gain in information per CPU-second and the clearest route to adaptation within a life.
Modifications:

- Draw the epoch parameters from the same family distribution as T-family, so one mechanism covers both kinds of variety.
- Add a genes_blind fork after a switch as the adaptation readout.
It needs user approval as a task decision.

The audit's verdict calls this a must: torch.randn and glibc's FMA paths differ by CPU. Without it, results and resumed runs on rented boxes are not bitwise.

3. The life-length draw as a compute lever. T 1536 lives take 52% of generation time, and in SPECK T 512 lives gave 1.2-1.4x more selection information per CPU-second. Longer lives also punish overgrowth, and D-episodes wants longer lives. Nobody weighed this trade-off. 4. A scale criterion for task design, which answers the user's reframing question:
- Cost is linear in cell-time.
- Noise is Poisson in scored events.
- Development is paid once per life.
So rank candidate worlds by selection information per CPU-second (per-life SD, or split-half reliability, divided by CPU per life) next to the computation niche. Favour worlds with many scored events per life, competitive small bodies, and many situations per development (epochs). Note that mixing worlds itself raised reliability from 0.18 to about 0.5.

FIRE broadcasts, chemistry packets and notices scale with contacts, so cells that use radius 2 could cost about 1.5-2x per life. Its price per length should reflect that, and the radius gene should come after fast conduction and face gains, which together cover latency and direction.
